jobs.title: Site Reliability Engineer
jobs.description:
Who Are We?

Prolaio believes that continuous learning and collaboration can make a significant difference in how heart care is administered. We are creating smarter ways to address heart disease and heart risks by uniting patients, care teams, and researchers on a secure, technology-enabled platform that drives clinical innovation and offers a path towards better patient outcomes.
This is precision cardiology, and we know it’s within reach.

What Will You Do?

The Overview

The Site Reliability Engineer (SRE) will ensure that Prolaio’s cardiovascular data platform reliably captures, transports, and delivers continuous biosensor data from participants to the clinical researchers and trial sponsors who depend on it. In this role, you will build and operate the monitoring, service level objectives, incident response, and automation needed to keep critical data flows healthy, identify failures before they impact studies, and ensure that device downtime never goes unnoticed simply because a shipment record says a device was delivered.

This role is ideal for a self-starter who thrives at the intersection of software reliability, connected devices, and clinical data. You will investigate incidents across the full participant-to-platform stack, combining service telemetry with device data and participant reports to determine whether an issue originated with the hardware, phone, firmware, mobile application, connectivity, or the platform itself. You will turn those investigations into durable improvements, automating manual checks, strengthening observability, reducing operational toil, and building the reliability practices that keep Prolaio’s clinical data complete and trustworthy at scale.

The Specifics

Build monitoring that treats missing data as a failure rather than a quiet day — freshness, volume and quality checks that verify delivery from outside the system instead of trusting a job's exit code.
Define and maintain SLIs, SLOs and error budgets for customer-facing data services, and report attainment honestly, including when the news is bad.
Join the on-call rotation, run incident response, and write blameless postmortems that produce owned follow-up actions.
Investigate device failures end to end: correlate discharge curves, Bluetooth disconnects and wear detection against the participant's complaint, and establish or exonerate each candidate cause on evidence.
Treat the fleet as a population — failure rates per device-month, clustering by build lot, firmware version or site — rather than as a queue of individual tickets.
Close the loop. When an analysis cannot reach a verdict, name the missing metric or threshold and route it back into the diagnostics pipeline so the next case is answerable from telemetry alone.
Build reliability tooling in Python and SQL on BigQuery, and keep monitors and probes defined as code rather than configured by hand.
Retire manual checks by automating them. Operational toil should shrink quarter over quarter, not accumulate.

Why Prolaio?

Impactful Work:
You will join in the fight against heart failure (HF) and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) with the goal of extending and saving the lives of our patients while also being at the forefront of changing the healthcare industry through technology.
Innovative Environment:
You will be part of an organization doing something that’s never been done before.
Professional Growth:
You will join a growing team and have a substantial impact on our daily and future operations with the opportunity to continuously learn and grow.
Collaborative Team:
You will be part of a team of collaborative, curious, and committed individuals focused on the collective good, inclusiveness, scientific excellence, and advancing digital health for cardiology.

Who You Are?

Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Biomedical Engineering or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
2–5 years in reliability engineering, production operations, hardware or systems test, field failure analysis, or data engineering — in a role where you were accountable for something that had to keep working.
Working SQL and Python: able to pull a dataset, characterize it, and defend the query behind a number.
Experience with a cloud data platform (Google Cloud and BigQuery preferred; AWS or Azure equivalents are fine).
Ability to write up a technical investigation clearly — what was observed, what was ruled out and how, and what remains unknown.

Additional Qualifications (Nice to Haves)

Hands-on exposure to Bluetooth Low Energy (GATT services and characteristics, connection intervals, pairing and bonding, disconnect behaviour), Wi-Fi or cellular data standards — and how each one fails in the field rather than how it is specified to behave.
Battery and power behaviour: discharge characterisation, charge-state interpretation, and telling a measurement artefact from a real capacity defect.
Formal reliability method — FMEA and risk priority numbers, FRACAS practice, and standards such as IEC 60812 or ISO 13485.
Observability tooling (Datadog, Grafana or similar) and synthetic monitoring.
Android device telemetry, mobile application diagnostics, or embedded firmware experience.
Prior work in medtech, digital health, clinical trials or another regulated, patient-facing environment.

Why You’ll Love Working Here

: Competitive salary, performance bonus, and equity so you can share in what we build.

Flexible Spending Perks:

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Blockchain
jobs.description:
About HIFI

HIFI is a stablecoin infrastructure company building technology for the next-generation of financial products. We build tools for payments and tokenized money products across money movement, cards, and capital markets. Institutions and enterprises already use our platform and APIs to move billions of dollars in production environments around the world, and we are still early.

Founded in 2022, our organization is flat and our team is talent dense. We work in person at our office in Flatiron and are intentional about who we work with. We've raised $37 million from world-class investors, including a Series A led by Left Lane Capital.

About The Team

HIFI's engineering team builds the payments infrastructure that fintechs and financial institutions use to move money on stablecoin rails. The team owns the APIs, ledger, and on-chain systems behind every payment HIFI processes, and works closely with product and compliance to make sure that infrastructure is reliable, secure, and ready for regulated use. As HIFI's volume grows and more institutions build on our platform, this team will decide how stablecoin payments hold up at the scale and standard that traditional financial infrastructure is held to.

As a Blockchain Engineer
at HIFI you will help own on-chain systems day to day. You'll build and maintain the integrations, smart contracts, and wallet infrastructure that connect HIFI's payments products to the chains and stablecoins we support. This is a hands-on role with real ownership: you'll design how funds move and settle on-chain, work with the rest of engineering to connect those flows to our ledger and APIs, and partner with compliance on controls like wallet screening and transaction monitoring. You'll also be the person the team relies on to judge when a new chain or protocol is ready for production use.

What You Will Build

Wallet infrastructure, including key management, transaction signing, and orchestration across custodial and programmatic wallets.
Onchain transaction handling across EVM chains and the other networks we support, including gas, nonce management, and retries.
Stablecoin minting, burning, and settlement logic that connects USDC and other stablecoins to fiat rails for our on-ramp and off-ramp products.
Integrations with centralized and decentralized exchanges for swaps and liquidity routing, and cross-chain bridging between networks.
A double-entry ledger that keeps onchain balances, banking partners, and customer accounts in sync, with automated reconciliation.
Event listeners, confirmation tracking, and webhooks that give our platform and customers real-time visibility into onchain activity.
Idempotent transaction pipelines with failure recovery and screening hooks, so money moves correctly even when something goes wrong.

You might be a fit if

3+ years of software engineering experience, including at least 1 to 2 years building blockchain systems in production.
Deep familiarity with EVM chains, including transaction lifecycles, gas mechanics, common failure modes, and enough Solidity to read and integrate contracts.
Experience with wallet architecture, such as custody models, signing services, or MPC and HSM-backed setups.
Strong backend fundamentals, including API design, data modeling, and handling consistency and concurrency in distributed systems.
You build financial systems with reconciliation and audit trails by default.
You communicate clearly in code review and in writing.

Nice to have

Experience with stablecoin infrastructure such as Circle, or with connecting onchain and fiat settlement.
Hands-on work with CEX APIs, DEX protocols like Uniswap, or bridge integrations.
Experience building ledgers or double-entry accounting systems.
Exposure to compliance engineering, such as transaction monitoring, address screening, or Travel Rule tooling.
Experience with non-EVM chains like Solana or Tron.
Familiarity with traditional money movement, including ACH, wires, and how funds settle between banks and processors.
Early-stage startup experience building and running a system from scratch.

Why This Role Matters

Every payment HIFI processes eventually settles on-chain, and the institutions behind those payments expect them to work as reliably as a wire or an ACH transfer. This is a chance to build the on-chain systems that hold stablecoin payments to that standard, and to shape how regulated money moves on public blockchains while that infrastructure is still being defined.

Additional Requirement

Must be within a commutable distance from our office and able to work in person most days of the week.

We also provide reasonable accommodations during the hiring process.

The hard part isn't the model call. It's governability — making AI accountable enough to trust with real deal flow. Who is the AI acting for? What is it allowed to do? What happens when it's wrong? In a regulated industry, those aren't side questions. They're the engineering problem.We've been answering them inside our own wholesale brokerage for years. That's where we test whether the model actually produces more reliable, scalable, and consistent service. If it doesn't work for us, it doesn't deserve to be packaged for the market. Now we're packaging it.
The roleSoftware Engineers sit at the point where Third Plane, our platform, meets the messy reality of our agency. You own the outcome at QuoteWell, the internal customer. You also own the signal back to the rest of the company.
A typical month: you're embedded at QuoteWell, working alongside our operators. You're identifying the workflows where heroics break down — submissions, renewals, follow-up, the work that today depends on someone's memory — and you're building governed AI execution into those workflows. You're calibrating where humans stay (judgment, relationships, accountability) and where the system carries the standard (follow-through, coordination, attention).
The hardest and most interesting part: making it trustworthy. How AI decisions get reviewed, attributed, and defended. That work is what determines whether any of this can actually live in production.
Then you bring it all back. Engineering, Product, and Design need to know what generalizes and what doesn't, so the platform compounds across every customer instead of fragmenting into one-offs. You're the conduit.
What you'll doBuild governed AI workflows — integrating with AMS, carrier portals, email, and the systems our agency actually runs onIdentify which parts of the agency's operation can be made system-governed without losing the judgment that has to stay with peopleDesign the review, attribution, and override patterns that let a regulated business trust the systemCarry field signal back to Engineering, Product, and Design so the platform scales rather than splinters

Insurance is a financial supply chain puzzle, and we expect you to want to understand itGenuine hustle. The kind of person who walks into Monday with a working prototype of something they spotted on FridayWillingness to travel
What you getA real production model to build on, not a slide deck. Our wholesale brokerage is the proof point — you're scaling something that already works.Direct mentorship from Joey, who built and ran applied AI at Palantir before this.An industry that matters. jobs.description:
THE POSITION

Our roster has an opening with your name on it

As a Software Engineer within FanDuel’s Trading Solutions team, you will be an essential part of a cross functional agile team that directly impacts our business. You will work collaboratively with a team to implement creative, high-quality solutions, scope effort and timelines, and balance priorities of our stakeholders and engineering needs. This team will work closely to deliver exceptionally high-quality software, while taking pride and ownership in testing, deploying, monitoring, and maintaining that software. Our engineers own every part of the software delivery lifecycle.

You will work directly with quantitative analysts at FanDuel to improve the major US sports platforms. You will be a domain expert on price modeling implementation and how that fits into the larger Risk and Trading landscape. You will go beyond the software developer role and will be called upon to identify opportunities yourself in the quantitative space to innovate through technology.

THE GAME PLAN

Everyone on our team has a part to play

You are a significant and autonomous contributor. Your work is consistently of high quality. You solve difficult problems, applying appropriate technologies and best practices. You work with your team to invent, design and build software that is stable and performant. You limit the use of short-term workarounds. You do things with the proper level of complexity the first time (or at least minimize incidental complexity). You create flexible software without over-engineering. You make appropriate trade-offs, re-use where possible, and are judicious about introducing dependencies. You are efficient with resource usage (e.g., system hardware, database, memory/CPU, etc).

We are looking for engineers to actively engage in technical discussions, assist in designing and implementing solutions, and deliver constant improvements to our systems. We want you to be excited about constantly learning and driving your professional development. You should have many of the following skills and be eager to build the skills you don’t!:

You work in project ideas with stakeholders, and peers.
You own parts of product and technology & become subject matter experts.
You write simple and extendable code following standards and best practices. You test your code thoroughly.
You help balance customer requirements with the team requirements.
You help your team evolve by actively participating in the code review process, design discussions, team planning, and ticket/metric/COE reviews.
You classify, store, and handle data in accordance with FanDuel policies.
You track security risks and mitigate and/or escalate them in a timely manner.
You focus on operational excellence, constructively identifying problems and proposing solutions.
You take on projects and make software enhancements that improve the team software and processes.
You work to resolve the root cause of complex problems, leaving software better and easier to maintain than when you found it.
On-call rotation where required. You provide excellent customer support.
You keep yourself up to date with market standards, open-source frameworks.
Creative problem-solving ability.
A passion for learning and always getting better.
Most importantly, you are; humble, pragmatic, self-managed, thirsty for knowledge, never satisfied and always challenging the norm. Responsible for the state of the code you both inherit and produce.

THE STATS

What we’re looking for in our next teammate

Degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, or related discipline preferred.
3 or more years of industry experience in an Engineering field, Machine Learning, Data Science, Finance Engineering, or Statistics preferred.
Proficient in building services with a modern OOP language (C# experience is beneficial).
Understanding of performance, hardware, and lower-level memory management (C, C++, or Rust experience is beneficial).
A fundamental understanding of data structures and algorithms.
Experience working with CI/CD pipeline tooling (BuildKite and GitHub Actions knowledge is beneficial).
Experience working with cloud-based infrastructure and technologies.
Knowledge of infrastructure as code is nice to have, notably Terraform and Helm.
Experience interacting and designing relational databases.
Experience with streaming technologies, like Kafka, is nice to have.
Ability to document code, research, and designs clearly.
Proficiency in translating requirements into design and developing applications.
Understanding of containers (e.g. Docker), and orchestration (Kubernetes).
Experience with unit testing, testing tools, integrating testing and best-quality practices into an SDLC.
Experience working in an Agile environment.

FanDuel Group is the premier mobile gaming company in the United States and Canada. FanDuel Group consists of a portfolio of leading brands across mobile wagering including: America’s #1 Sportsbook, FanDuel Sportsbook; its leading iGaming platform, FanDuel Casino; the industry’s unquestioned leader in horse racing and advance-deposit wagering, FanDuel Racing; and its daily fantasy sports product.

In addition, FanDuel Group operates FanDuel TV, its broadly distributed linear cable television network and FanDuel TV+, its leading direct-to-consumer OTT platform. FanDuel Group has a presence across all 50 states, Canada, and Puerto Rico.

jobs.title: Sr. Software Engineer, Kernels/CUDA (C++)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.
SR. SOFTWARE ENGINEER, KERNELS/CUDA (C++)
We are building one of the world’s largest AI supercomputers from the ground up. As part of the Compute Infrastructure team, you will own both the raw GPU supercomputer and the platform layer that runs on top of it. You will work across the full stack — from low-level GPU kernel optimizations and Linux kernel internals to massive-scale orchestration and virtualization — to make training and inference at SpaceXSI as fast, reliable, and scalable as possible.
This is a broad, high-impact role that combines hardcore supercompute and compute infrastructure work. Your contributions will directly accelerate Grok’s training speed and overall AI progress.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Design, build, and optimize massive GPU clusters for extreme-scale training and inference workloads
Develop and tune low-level CUDA kernels (GeMM, Attention, etc.), using CUTLASS, Tensor Cores, and Nsight for maximum performance
Profile, debug, and eliminate bottlenecks across GPU memory hierarchy, networking fabric, filesystems, and multi-GPU operation
Collaborate closely with AI research teams to deliver production-grade performance and scalability

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:
5+ years of experience with low-level system programming in C/C++

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:
Deep low-level systems programming (C/C++/PTX/SASS)
Strong experience with large-scale GPU clusters or distributed compute infrastructure at production scale
Hands-on work with GPU kernel optimization (CUTLASS, custom kernels, Nsight profiling)
Track record of building or running high-performance infrastructure for AI workloads (training or inference platforms)
Ability to reason from first principles and optimize for both memory-bound and compute-bound scenarios

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:
$200,000 - $375,000 USD
Base salary is just one part of our total rewards package at SpaceXSI, which also includes equity, comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short & long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and various other discounts and perks.
SpaceXSI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our  Recruitment Privacy Notice.

jobs.title: Expert: Interactive Coding, Site Reliability Engineering (Contract, Remote)
jobs.description:
**About Patronus AI**
---------------------

Patronus AI is a frontier lab developing simulation research and infrastructure to accelerate progress toward human-aligned AGI. We are on a mission to simulate all of the world's intelligence.

We are the team behind some of the earliest and most influential research in AI evaluation like FinanceBench, Lynx, SimpleSafetyTests, CopyrightCatcher, Humanity's Last Exam, and more. We are formerly AI researchers and engineers from companies like Meta AI, Amazon AGI, and Google. Our customers include foundation model labs and Fortune 500 enterprises like Adobe. We are backed by top-tier investors like Lightspeed Venture Partners, Notable Capital, Stanford University, Noam Brown, Gokul Rajaram, and more.

**At a glance**
---------------

* **Engagement:** Independent contractor, fully remote. Live screen-share sessions with our researchers plus short asynchronous write-ups.
* **Pay:** $150 per hour. The trial session is paid.
* **Commitment:** About 10 hours per week, 1 to 3 months to start, with extension for strong performers.
* **Start:** Rolling
* **Location:** Remote, any country, with a few hours of overlap with US or EU working hours.

**The role**
------------

You'll work live with our research team on production-style reliability scenarios in a sandboxed stack: Kubernetes, Prometheus and Grafana, a log system, Helm and Terraform, and CI/CD. You solve the scenario the way you would on call, explain your reasoning as you go, tell us where the scenario doesn't match real operations, and help define what a correct resolution looks like.

Each session starts from a scenario we provide. You investigate it on a shared screen, fix or mitigate it, and then write a short note on how you approached it. Your work becomes evaluation and training data for frontier models.

You don't need an AI background. You do need to be the kind of engineer who reads the dashboard before touching the config, and who can say out loud why a tempting fix is the wrong one.

**Areas we're hiring for**
--------------------------

Each area is defined by the systems you run, so you should fit exactly one. If you work across two, apply under the one where you spend most of your time.

* **Incident response and on-call.** Engineers on a production rotation who triage alerts, read metrics, logs and traces, find root cause, mitigate, roll back and write the post-mortem. **Typical titles:** Site Reliability Engineer, Production Engineer, On-Call Engineer, Platform Engineer.
* **Platform and infrastructure.** Engineers who own clusters, deploy pipelines and infrastructure as code: Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, CI/CD, networking and capacity. **Typical titles:** Infrastructure Engineer, DevOps Engineer, Platform Engineer, Cloud Engineer.
* **Observability.** Engineers who build and tune the monitoring itself: Prometheus and PromQL, Grafana dashboards and alert rules, Loki or ELK, OpenTelemetry tracing, SLOs and error budgets. **Typical titles:** Observability Engineer, Monitoring Engineer, Site Reliability Engineer (Observability).

**What you'll do**
------------------

* Work through incident, debugging and infrastructure-change scenarios live with a researcher: reading dashboards and logs, writing PromQL and LogQL, fixing Helm and Kubernetes configuration, rolling back bad deploys and writing post-mortems.
* Explain your reasoning as you work, including the fixes you considered and rejected.
* Review scenarios we have drafted and say plainly what is unrealistic, too easy or underspecified.
* Help write the acceptance criteria for each scenario, including the tempting wrong moves an engineer under pressure might make.
* Write short notes after each session on how you approached the problem and what you verified.
* Work in reviewer feedback within agreed turnaround times, and flag guideline gaps or edge cases you run into.

**Who we're looking for**
-------------------------

**Required**

* 3+ years running production systems in at least one of the areas above, including time on an on-call rotation within the last two years. You did the work yourself; managing the team is not enough.
* Hands-on with Kubernetes, Prometheus and Grafana (or Datadog or New Relic), a log stack such as Loki, ELK or Splunk, infrastructure as code such as Terraform and Helm, and a CI/CD system.
* Comfortable in Python, Go or Bash and at reading unfamiliar codebases.
* Able to explain your reasoning out loud while you work, in clear professional English.
* Reliable availability for scheduled live sessions and the habit of showing the evidence behind every conclusion.

**Nice to have**

* Experience writing runbooks, post-mortems, SLO definitions or incident training material.
* Familiarity with how AI coding agents fail on operations work.

**Our standards**
-----------------

* All solutions, write-ups and reviews are your own work. LLM-generated code or text is not permitted.
* Scenarios and solutions must be original. Nothing may be copied from published or easily searchable sources.
* Never include code, configuration, runbooks or incident details from a current or former employer or client, or anything covered by an NDA. All systems and scenarios are fictional, and all work is your own.
* Quality is judged on correctness, clarity of reasoning and reviewer agreement, not on speed or volume.

**How hiring works**
--------------------

* Short AI interview and resume review
* One paid trial session, scored against a fixed quality checklist
* Onboarding and your first project

We celebrate diversity in our workplace, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (in

jobs.description:
***A day in the life:***

We are seeking a Front End Developer to build high-quality, accessible user interfaces with a strong focus on Section 508 compliance. This role involves front-end development, accessibility testing, and remediation, using Section 508 standards and screen reader technologies to identify and resolve accessibility issues. You will work alongside an Agile team of software developers, systems engineers, and product owners to develop, test, and deliver user-friendly interfaces that are accessible to individuals with disabilities.

Key Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

* Design, develop, and maintain accessible front-end components and user interfaces compliant with Section 508 and WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA standards
* Conduct accessibility testing using JAWS and other screen readers, identifying and resolving issues with keyboard navigation, focus management, ARIA, color contrast, and semantic HTML.
* Perform manual and automated accessibility audits, document findings, and prepare compliance reports as needed.
* Collaborate with UX/UI designers, developers, and product owners to incorporate accessibility early in the design process and provide guidance on accessible design practices.
* Work with QA and DevOps to integrate automated accessibility testing tools (axe-core, Pa11y, Lighthouse) into CI/CD pipelines for continuous compliance monitoring.
* Participate in Agile ceremonies, including sprint planning and demos, and communicate accessibility requirements and tradeoffs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

***What you bring to the table:***

* Bachelor's degree from an accredited university in Computer Science or a related technical field OR 4 additional years of experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.
* Levels:
  + Mid: 3+ years of relevant experience in software development/engineering.
  + Senior: 8+ years of relevant experience in software development/engineering.
  + SME: 12+ years of relevant experience in software development/engineering.
* Experience developing front-end applications using modern JavaScript frameworks (Vue preferred).
* Hands-on experience with JAWS screen reader and familiarity with other assistive technologies.
* Strong knowledge of Section 508, WCAG 2.1/2.2 (Levels A/AA), and ARIA best practices.
* Experience with semantic HTML, accessible forms, keyboard navigation, and focus management.
* Proficiency with accessibility testing and auditing tools (axe DevTools, WAVE, Pa11y, Lighthouse).
* Experience with Git version control and Agile collaboration tools (Jira, Confluence).
* Active TS/SCI with Polygraph level of security clearance.

*Bonus Skills:*

* Experience producing VPATs/Accessibility Conformance Reports for federal agency review.
* Familiarity with integrating automated accessibility checks into CI/CD pipelines (e.g., GitLab CI/CD).
* Experience with Cypress or similar tools for automated UI/accessibility test scripting.
* Familiarity with Cloud-based architecture and deployment (Amazon Web Services).

jobs.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.description:
### **RESULTS. INNOVATION. VALUES. ACCOUNTABILITY.**

That's RIVA.

We're a mission-driven IT services company and systems integrator supporting digital transformation and modernization for federal government agencies. Since 2009, we've partnered with our customers to solve complex challenges through smart, practical innovation to deliver real outcomes where they matter most. Our teams are made up of industry-leading experts who are passionate about doing great work and making a difference. We don't just develop solutions, we support efforts that strengthen communities and serve the public good.  
  
RIVA's culture is built on four core values: Results, Innovation, Values, and Accountability. They guide how we work, how we collaborate, and how we measure success. Our employee-first approach is rooted in trust, ownership, and meaningful work. By investing in our people and fostering a flexible, supportive environment, employees have the opportunity to grow their skills, contribute ideas, and make an impact from day one. all while supporting missions that matter.

### **POSITION OVERVIEW**

RIVA Solutions seeks an AI Subject Matter Expert to support the USPTO P-TACTS program, the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) case tracking and electronic filing system. You will design, build, and evaluate production AI solutions that turn unstructured  
legal filings into reliable, structured data. A current example: a pipeline that reads PTAB petitions, institution decisions, and final written decisions, then extracts trial-level and claim-level outcomes. The team measures the pipeline against analyst-labeled ground truth. The output supports reporting that PTAB delivers to Congress. You will work mainly in Python on Databricks, inside a secured federal environment. Development runs on remote instances through VPN. LLM access runs through an agency AI gateway, and approved models trail the commercial market. You will work directly with government stakeholders and engineers to turn mission needs into working, maintainable, and measurable applications.

### **WHAT YOU WILL DO**

* Build LLM pipelines that extract structured data from long, unstructured legal documents.
* Decide when a task needs a flexible agentic harness and when it needs a constrained, step-by-step pipeline. Build either one.
* Validate model outputs against schemas, allowed values, and business rules. Handle failures without losing records silently.
* Design evaluations against ground truth. Choose the right metric for the problem, run error analysis, and report results in plain terms.
* Use AI coding tools such as Claude Code every day to build, test, and review code.
* Keep pipelines stable as approved models change, using version pinning, regression test sets, and prompt versioning.
* Advise the customer on future use cases, including fine-tuning small language models or adapters when the data supports it.

### **MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, or a related field.
* 5+ years of applied ML, data science, or AI engineering experience, including 2+ years building applications on large language models in production or near-production settings.
* Strong Python skills, including data work with pandas or PySpark.
* Solid ML fundamentals: classification, train and test splits, overfitting, data leakage, and model selection.
* Hands-on evaluation skill: precision, recall, F1, confusion matrices, class imbalance, and comparison to labeled ground truth.
* Production experience building with LLM APIs, including structured output, tool calling, and prompt design.
* Experience building or debugging an agent harness, and the judgment to explain when a structured pipeline is the better choice.
* Experience validating LLM output with schemas (for example, Pydantic or JSON Schema), retries, and exception handling.
* Daily use of AI coding assistants such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or GitHub Copilot.
* Hands-on experience building and running ML or LLM workloads on Databricks or a major cloud platform (AWS, Azure, or GCP). Examples: data pipelines in PySpark or notebooks, calling hosted models through Databricks Model Serving, Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker, Azure OpenAI, Azure Machine Learning, or Vertex AI, and tracking experiments in MLflow.
* AWS Certified Machine Learning Engineer - Associate, or an equivalent cloud ML certification. An active AWS Certified Machine Learning - Specialty also counts.
* Eligibility to obtain a USPTO Public Trust and authorization to work in the U.S.

### **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Databricks experience, including Jobs, Delta Lake, MLflow, and Unity Catalog. PyTorch experience, including fine-tuning small language models or training LoRA adapters.
* AWS experience, including Amazon Bedrock.
* Information extraction from scanned or long documents, including OCR and layout analysis.
* Retrieval augmented generation and vector databases.
* MLOps experience: pipeline orchestration, evaluation sets run in CI, and monitoring of output quality over time.
* Experience working through an enterprise AI gateway with cost tracking and request filtering.
* Databricks Certified Machine Learning Professional, Databricks Certified Machine Learning Associate, Databricks Certified Generative AI Engineer Associate, AWS Certified Machine Learning Engineer - Associate, or an equivalent cloud certification.
* Experience with USPTO, PTAB, or patent and legal data.
* Prior delivery on federal government contracts, including FISMA Moderate systems.

### **EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY & ACCOMMODATION**

We believe great teams are built from different backgrounds, perspectives, and lived experiences, and we mean that beyond the buzzwords.

RIVA is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, and any other characteristic protected by law.

The Media Group at NBCU supports a powerhouse collection of consumer-first brands including Peacock, NBC, Bravo, NBC Sports, and NBCU International. With unequalled scale, our teams make the most out of every opportunity to collaborate and learn from one another. We’re always looking for ways to innovate faster, accelerate our growth and consistently offer the very best in consumer experience. But most of all, we’re backed by a culture of respect. We're looking for a Roku Software Engineer to own and evolve our Roku channel, from the SceneGraph UI layer down to the playback pipeline and the APIs that feed it. Roku is one of the largest surfaces in our streaming footprint, and it's also the most constrained: the same channel has to feel fast on a top-tier Roku Ultra and on a five-year-old Roku Express with a fraction of the memory.

This role is for someone who treats those constraints as the interesting part of the job. You'll be measuring texture memory and node counts, chasing down rebuffer events in HLS manifests, and working with backend teams to shape the microservice responses that make a channel launch in under two seconds instead of six.

* Design, build, and ship features in BrightScript and SceneGraph, with a strong bias toward maintainable, well-factored component architecture rather than monolithic screens.
* Own video playback quality end to end: startup time, ABR behavior, seek responsiveness, trick play, DRM handshakes, and graceful failure and recovery.
* Profile and tune channel performance against real device constraints: memory ceilings on legacy hardware, render thread contention, task node usage, image and texture budgets, and cold-start latency.
* Instrument and act on QoE telemetry (startup time, rebuffer ratio, exit-before-video-start, bitrate distribution), and drive those numbers down over time.
* Partner with backend teams to define and refine the microservice and BFF APIs that power the channel: catalog, playback authorization, entitlement, continue-watching, recommendations, and search.
* Implement and maintain Roku platform integrations: deep linking, Roku Search and content feeds, Continue Watching, Roku Pay / Instant Signup, and the Roku Advertising Framework.
* Build and maintain internal tooling and automation scripts in JavaScript/TypeScript: build and packaging steps, feed and manifest validators, release utilities, device-farm and smoke-test harnesses, and whatever else removes manual toil from the team's day.
* Own the channel's CI/CD pipeline: automated builds, test execution, static analysis, artifact packaging, sideloading to test devices, and promotion through environments. You treat pipeline code as real code, with the same review and maintenance standards.
* Shepherd releases through Roku channel certification, including performance and memory requirements, and manage the beta-to-production promotion process.
* Establish and uphold engineering standards: code review, automated testing, static analysis, and clear documentation.
* Debug production issues across the stack using the Roku debug console, profiler, ECP, and network capture, and turn root causes into durable fixes.

  
**Qualifications**  

* 3+ years of software engineering experience, including shipping production Roku channels with BrightScript and SceneGraph.
* Demonstrated experience with performance tuning on constrained devices. You can talk specifically about a time you cut memory usage, reduced startup latency, or eliminated frame drops, and how you measured it.
* Strong grounding in software engineering best practices: separation of concerns, testability, meaningful abstractions, code review discipline, and refactoring as a habit rather than a project.
* Hands-on experience with video playback and streaming formats: HLS and/or DASH, adaptive bitrate behavior, manifest structure, buffering strategy, and DRM (Widevine and PlayReady on Roku).
* Practical experience consuming and integrating with RESTful APIs in a microservice architecture, including pagination, caching, retry and backoff strategies, error contracts, and versioning.
* Working proficiency in JavaScript and TypeScript (Node.js) for internal tooling and build automation. You can write a maintainable CLI or script that other engineers will actually use, not just a one-off.

Plug was founded in 2023 and is led by former Tesla executives. It is backed by a $20M Series A from Lightspeed Venture Partners. We're building the most AI-native startup team in Los Angeles: operators, engineers and ML researchers building the transaction rails for the fast-growing used EV market.

**WHY PLUG**
------------

* You'll help build the biggest infrastructure opportunity in automotive.
* You'll work on a platform built only for EVs, with nothing adapted from legacy automotive.
* You'll be part of an AI-native company that is rethinking how work gets done.
* You'll work directly with operators who have scaled multi-billion-dollar businesses in automotive, EV and marketplaces.
* You'll work alongside a small, senior team, with high autonomy and a direct line to company outcomes.

**THE OPPORTUNITY**
-------------------

Every car on Plug starts with a number: what is this EV worth today, and what will a dealer pay for it tomorrow? Those numbers come from our models. They draw on auction results, market data, vehicle telematics and battery health. As volume grows, our models have to get more accurate, update faster, and be easier to trust and explain.

You'll join our Intelligence team and work alongside our ML engineer and data team, who built the models behind pricing and battery health. Together you'll take those models further: sharper price and volume forecasts, battery state-of-health models built from telematics, and LLM pipelines that pull structured data out of vehicle, title and inspection documents.

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**
------------------

* Work with the team to build, improve and run in production the models behind instant offers, auction pricing and sell-through: valuation, price and volume forecasting, and demand signals.
* Develop battery state-of-health and vehicle-condition models from telematics and other time-series data, which is often noisy, sparse or only partly labeled.
* Take models through the full lifecycle together with the team: feature pipelines on our Snowflake/dbt stack, training, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, drift detection and retraining.
* Evaluate models by statistical accuracy and by business outcomes such as offer acceptance, margin and arbitration rate, and help build the feedback loops that connect the two.
* Bring in LLMs where they work better than traditional models, for example pulling structured data out of vehicle, title and inspection documents. Build the evaluations that show whether they hold up.
* Strengthen how the team works as it grows: experiment tracking, model registry, reproducible training and code review for ML work. Share what you know, pair on hard problems, and learn from the people who know our data best.

**WHAT YOU'LL BRING**
---------------------

* 5+ years building and shipping machine learning systems, with several models running in production that you supported well after launch, not just trained.
* Strong Python, plus deep experience with at least one modern ML framework (PyTorch, scikit-learn, XGBoost/LightGBM or similar).
* Practical experience with forecasting, regression or pricing problems on tabular and time-series data.
* Solid grounding in statistics and experiment design: validation strategy, leakage, calibration, and knowing when a metric is lying to you.
* Comfort with real-world, messy data and strong SQL. Experience with a modern data stack (Snowflake, dbt or similar) is a plus.
* Hands-on experience building with LLMs: tool use, retrieval, structured output, and above all evaluation.
* You work agent-first. You've built your own tooling around coding agents, such as skills, MCP servers, custom workflows or evals.
* A habit of writing things down: design docs, model cards and runbooks that others can pick up.
* You enjoy being part of a small team: pairing, reviewing each other's work and sharing credit.
* Comfort building inside systems other people designed. You can disagree, make your case and then ship the agreed plan.
* High agency in an ambiguous, fast-moving startup. You find the most valuable problem and ship against it without waiting for a perfect spec.
* BS or MS in a quantitative field (computer science, statistics, engineering, physics, applied math) or equivalent experience.

### **Nice to have**

* Experience with vehicle, marketplace, auction, lending or insurance pricing data.
* Experience with sensor or telematics data, battery modeling or other physical-systems data.
* Experience with transfer learning, multi-task learning or model distillation.
* Experience with ML or LLM serving on a budget for latency and cost.

-----------------------------

PracHub is hiring for work on LandOffer.

LandOffer is a startup working on a practical problem: finding relevant jobs takes time, and applying often means entering the same information again and again.

Our product brings job listings together, helps candidates find matches based on their resumes and preferences, and offers a free Chrome extension for application autofill. Job seekers can also connect an AI assistant to review matches and apply to jobs they approve.

We want to make that experience more useful and less repetitive. Learn about the product at https://landoffer.ai/.

About the role

We are looking for a Junior Software Engineer to improve how people discover relevant jobs and complete applications. You will work on scoped product features, investigate bugs, and make changes that are easy to test and maintain.

What you will do

- Build and improve web features for browsing jobs, reviewing matches, and managing profile information.

- Investigate issues in application autofill and help make the extension work reliably across different forms.

- Work with APIs and data storage to keep information accurate across the product.

- Write tests for the behavior you change, review code, and document implementation decisions.

- Turn user feedback into clear bug reports and practical improvements.

- Working knowledge of a programming language and the ability to explain how your code behaves.

- Ability to use Git, investigate unfamiliar code, and communicate when a task is blocked.

Helpful experience

Browser extensions, JavaScript or TypeScript, SQL, automated testing, or projects involving search and structured data.

Why this role at our startup

You will work on the details that make a job-search product useful: how people find a relevant role, how an application form behaves, and what happens when something breaks. We are looking for someone who wants to understand the user's problem and can turn it into a small, reliable software improvement.

Join the team turning internet intelligence into real-world security outcomes. Built on the world's most comprehensive and accurate map of the Internet, the Censys Platform delivers real-time visibility and actionable intelligence needed to accelerate triage, investigate threats, hunt adversaries, and manage Internet exposure. We're trusted by half of the Fortune 500 and government agencies all around the world, and looking for people as passionate about the problems we're solving as we are.

At Censys, we're on a mission to provide best in class internet visibility and intelligence to the global security community. Our platform helps security teams uncover hidden threats, gain actionable insights, and build proactive defense strategies. Trusted by organizations worldwide, Censys cuts through the noise to surface the most critical risks, enabling teams to respond faster, and stay ahead of attackers. We're constantly pushing the boundaries of what's possible to help our customers see and secure the internet more clearly than ever before.

**Location:**

This position is **remote** within the United States or Canada.

**Role Summary:**

Censys is seeking a **Software Engineer II (Backend)** to join our Exposure Management team. Exposure Management is a growth product for Censys. It combines our map of the Internet with customer context to show security teams which exposures matter most, including the risk that reaches them through their suppliers via Supplier Risk Intelligence. We're looking for an engineer who can build the product APIs behind these experiences, taking a well-scoped feature from design through launch with input from senior engineers.

You'll work primarily in Go, pulling together data and services from other Censys teams and partnering with frontend engineers to deliver APIs that are fast, well-shaped, and easy to build on. As with all roles at Censys, we expect a strong customer focus, a collaborative mindset, and a desire to keep learning.

**What You'll Do:**

* Own small-to-medium product API features end to end, from technical design through launch, monitoring, and iteration
* Build and extend the public REST and gRPC APIs behind Exposure Management and Supplier Risk Intelligence, including the risk event endpoints that power SIEM integrations with Splunk, Google SecOps, and Microsoft Sentinel
* Partner with frontend engineers and product stakeholders on API contracts, filtering, pagination, and response shapes so customer-facing experiences stay fast and simple to build
* Work with other Censys teams to integrate their data and services through gRPC and GCP PubSub, and agree on interfaces that hold up as both sides evolve
* Profile and optimize API performance, from Postgres query plans and indexing to caching and payload size
* Write tests, add observability, and take release and on-call responsibility for the services you ship
* Bring customer feedback into design discussions and help onboard interns and newer engineers in your area

**What You'll Bring:**

* A positive attitude biased towards action and iterative problem solving, learning as we grow every step of the way.
* 4+ years of professional software engineering experience building backend services.
* Production experience with Go, or strong experience in another backend language (Python, Java) and the drive to become proficient in Go quickly.
* Experience designing and consuming REST or gRPC APIs, ideally ones consumed by a frontend application.
* Solid SQL skills and working knowledge of relational data modeling, indexing, and query performance.
* A track record of building maintainable software: tests enforced in CI, meaningful monitoring and alerting, and thoughtful code reviews.
* Clear written and verbal communication with engineers, product managers, and other teams.
* Curiosity and a willingness to pick up new domains, tools, and parts of the stack.

**What Sets You Apart:**

* Experience on security products, especially attack surface management, third-party risk or vulnerability management.
* Experience building APIs that external developers or partners integrate against (OpenAPI specs, versioning, webhooks).
* Experience with event-driven systems (GCP PubSub, Kafka) and patterns like idempotency and retries.
* Experience deploying containerized services on Kubernetes in GCP or AWS.
* Fluency with AI coding tools as a force multiplier for building better software.
* A working understanding of how the Internet works. DNS record types, WHOIS, and Certificate Subject Alternative Names (SANs) are familiar territory

jobs.title: Sr. Satellite Flight Software Engineer - TeraWave
jobs.description:
Application Close Date

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight! 

Blue Origin is pioneering the future of space-based communications with TeraWave, a revolutionary satellite communications network designed to deliver symmetrical data speeds of up to 6 Tbps anywhere on Earth. This multi-orbit constellation will consist of optically interconnected satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO) and medium Earth orbit (MEO), providing enterprise-grade connectivity for critical operations worldwide.

Job Description

This position is part of Blue Origin's TeraWave business unit, a newly announced satellite communications network designed to deliver symmetrical data speeds of up to 6 Tbps anywhere on Earth. TeraWave consists of 5,408 optically interconnected satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO) and medium Earth orbit (MEO), providing enterprise-grade connectivity for critical operations.

We are seeking a Senior Satellite Flight Software Engineer to provide technical expertise for TeraWave's Satellite Flight Software Subsystem. This role will be instrumental in developing robust, scalable flight software to support the growth of TeraWave into a 5,408-vehicle constellation. The ideal candidate is a hands-on flight software architect who will shape software architecture, drive cross-functional integration, and establish high standards for software quality, verification, security, and maintainability across the full flight software lifecycle.

Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To

Architect, design, develop, and integrate core flight software for a next-generation satellite platform
Define scalable, reusable, and platform-independent flight software frameworks, services, and design patterns to support multiple spacecraft configurations and future growth
Architect, develop, and evolve key flight software components including core services, command and data handling (C&DH), telemetry, health monitoring, and fault-management infrastructure
Establish software architecture standards, coding guidelines, design patterns, and review practices to ensure maintainability, reliability, and mission readiness
Partner closely with systems, avionics, GNC, communications, power, propulsion, thermal, payload, and autonomy teams to translate vehicle and subsystem-level requirements into robust software implementations
Conduct software design reviews, code reviews, and technical trade studies related to performance, fault tolerance, redundancy, scalability, and portability
Support software integration, verification, and validation in software-in-the-loop (SIL), hardware-in-the-loop (HIL), and other mission-representative test environments
Develop and improve software engineering infrastructure including build systems, CI/CD pipelines, automated test frameworks, and debugging/diagnostic tools
Contribute to technical documentation including software architecture descriptions, interface control documents, verification plans, and test procedures
Design and implement secure OTA software update capabilities for spacecraft, including validation, authenticated delivery, rollback, version control, and safe deployment in mission-critical on-orbit environments
Ensure flight software architecture and implementation incorporate cybersecurity principles such as secure communications, access control, interface hardening, and resilient software design

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or related technical field
8+ years of experience developing embedded software for spacecraft or other mission-critical real-time systems
Strong proficiency in C/C++ and Python
Experience with RTOS-based embedded software development with Embedded Linux, VxWorks, or QNX
Experience architecting and implementing complex flight software or mission-critical embedded software systems
Demonstrated technical depth across software design, implementation, and cross-functional integration
Experience with software lifecycle, configuration management, CI/CD, and verification/validation practices for mission-critical systems
Familiarity with communication protocols such as TCP/IP, UDP, CAN, I2C, SPI, and RS-422/485
Experience applying secure software development and cybersecurity best practices in embedded or mission-critical systems
Experience with embedded software testing methodologies

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical field
Experience with flight software frameworks such as core Flight System (cFS), F Prime, or similar
Experience developing software for satellite constellations, distributed space systems, or networked embedded platforms
Knowledge of satellite communications systems, spacecraft networking, and high-throughput data handling
Experience with software-in-the-loop (SIL), hardware-in-the-loop (HIL), and integrated spacecraft test environments
Experience with fault-tolerant computing, redundancy management, and resilient software architectures
Knowledge of radiation-hardened computing environments and software considerations for spaceflight
Experience with communication satellite systems, optical inter-satellite links, or related networking technologies
Experience designing secure over-the-air (OTA) software update mechanisms for embedded or mission-critical systems
Experience with software build systems, static analysis, code quality tooling, or automated verification frameworks for embedded systems

Why Blue Origin

At Blue Origin, we’re building the future of space-based connectivity through the TeraWave satellite communications network. As a Senior Satellite Flight Software Developer, you will help define the software architecture, engineering rigor, and technical foundation for a large-scale satellite constellation delivering high-performance, resilient global communications. Join a team solving complex, mission-critical problems at the intersection of spacecraft, software, networking, and system integration.

Join our team and be part of building a space-based network designed for tomorrow, where your expertise will directly contribute to creating a system that provides connectivity anywhere on Earth.

Base Pay Range For

CA applicants is $197,529.00 - $276,539.55 CO applicants is $181,626.00 - $254,275.35 WA applicants is $197,529.00 - $276,539.55

Other Site Ranges May Differ

Culture Statement

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

Export Control Regulations

Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Background Check

Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical

Benefits

Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details.

We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws. For more information on “Know Your Rights,” please see here.

Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation

Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at EEOCompliance@blueorigin.com. Responsibilities

The Multimedia Lab builds highly efficient, scalable video codec hardware solutions (FPGA and ASIC) from the ground up, serving billions of users. We bring together algorithm, architecture, software, firmware, and hardware design and verification expertise, designing high-performance video silicon IP across ASIC and SoC digital design, verification, and next-generation video codec hardware. Alongside the silicon work, we advance research in video understanding, perceptual quality assessment, image and video enhancement, and intelligent coding, including using multimodal models to improve coding decisions.

Quality, efficiency, and speed rarely improve together. Sharper images and better perceived quality usually cost bitrate, compute, or latency, and a technique that works in research does not always survive production at global scale.

You will take ideas from research through to silicon and production systems, where research decisions show up in the cost and quality of video across ByteDance's products.

About The Team

Our team is building industry-leading, highly efficient and scalable video codec hardware solutions (FPGA and ASIC) from the ground up to better serve our billions of users. We are looking for strong software and firmware engineers to design algorithms, C-model, and firmware for advanced video encoding and processing implemented in dedicated hardware accelerators. The successful candidate will be part of a fast-growing team that includes algorithm, architecture, software, firmware, and hardware design and verification experts with a dedication to technical excellence and a passion to build large-scale and high-performing video platforms and services.

We are looking for talented individuals to join our team. As a graduate, you will get opportunities to pursue bold ideas, tackle complex challenges, and unlock limitless growth. Successful candidates must be able to commit to an onboarding date by the end of the year. Please state your availability and graduation date clearly in your resume.

Responsibilities:

Design video analysis (ROI, content understanding, feature extraction etc.) and quality assessment algorithms, and participate in database creation, algorithm design/development/optimization, etc.
Participate in designing strategy and solutions for E2E video quality optimization with a combination of video analysis, processing and encoding algorithms, such as frame-level rate control.
Apply designed algorithms for VOD / Live streaming monitoring, data analysis, objective evaluation for algorithms etc.
Collaborate with Infra and multi-media platform teams to integrate algorithms into production workflows and validate their impact through A/B testing.

Minimum Qualification(s)

Individuals who are completing or have recently completed a PhD degree in computer science, electrical engineering, mathematics, statistics or a related discipline.
Excellent programming, debugging, and optimization skills in one or more general-purpose programming languages, including but not limited to: C/C++, Python.
Knowledge of image/video analysis algorithms or subjective/objective image/video quality algorithms, and state-of-the-art technologies, such as VMAF, PSNR, SSIM etc.
Hands-on experience with machine learning or deep learning and familiarity with frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.

Preferred Qualification(s)

Research and hands-on experience in designing, training, or applying deep learning models, including CNNs, Transformer architectures, and multimodal large language models (MLLMs).
Knowledge of common video processing algorithms, such as super-resolution, diffusion model, etc.
Knowledge of video codecs (AVC, HEVC, AV1, VP9, etc.) and experience in video codec design.
Experience with embedded processors like ARM Cortex M0/M3/M4 or RISC-V architecture, and real-time development in an RTOS environment.
Great communication skills, eager to learn, and always passionate about turning cutting-edge technologies into real-life use cases.

We are looking for a passionate and hands-on Robotics Software Engineer to join our team. You will play a key role in building and advancing the software modules that power our mobile robots, from navigation and control to sensor integration and system deployment. This is a role for someone who thrives at the intersection of software engineering and physical robotics, and who takes pride in writing code that runs reliably on real hardware in the real world.

Contribute to code reviews, technical documentation, and design discussions
Take increasing ownership of features from development through deployment

The AI and Automation Engineer designs, prototypes, builds, integrates, evaluates, and helps productionize AI-enabled and automation solutions that address defined business and project needs. Working within TRI’s AI and Digital Enablement capability, the AI and Automation Engineer translates qualified opportunities into working solutions using established AI models and services (focused on Azure/Foundry), agents, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), workflow automation, data integration, and other appropriate technologies. The role emphasizes rapid experimentation, integration, and measurable evaluation, including recognizing when conventional automation or existing technology provides a better solution than AI. 
This is an applied AI engineering role, not an AI research or model-development position. The AI and Automation Engineer is not expected to develop, train, or research new foundation models. Inste.ad, the engineer selects, configures, integrates, grounds, evaluates, and applies existing models and AI services within secure enterprise solutions. The engineer works closely with Business Liaisons, business SMEs, application developers, infrastructure, and security teams to move promising concepts from prototype through evaluation, pilot, and production. Current areas of emphasis include Microsoft Foundry and Azure AI services, RAG and enterprise knowledge solutions, AI agents, Power Platform automation, enterprise integration, and evaluation of solution quality, security, performance, cost, and business value. Software/application development experience, preferably Python plus API/integration development in C#.

Experience with LLM fine-tuning and model customization techniques, including dataset preparation, supervised fine-tuning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning (e.g., LoRA/QLoRA), and model evaluation to optimize performance, accuracy, and domain-specific capabilities.

Power Automate / Power Platform.

Azure application services and identity.

Agentic solution development. 
AI evaluation and observability. 
Clinical research, life sciences, regulatory or federal contracting experience. 
Experience with enterprise document/knowledge systems. 
Experience productionizing prototypes. 
Familiarity with regulated or validated environments. 
Experience applying AI to document intelligence, workflow automation, knowledge retrieval, QC or decision-support use cases.

jobs.title: Software Engineer II - Cloud-Native Agent Harness (Mecatl)
jobs.description:
Stacklok is led by CEO Craig McLuckie and CTO Joe Beda, two of the creators of Kubernetes. Kubernetes helped give enterprises more freedom over where and how they run software. Now we're bringing that same open approach to AI agents.

As AI agents take on more autonomous, long-running work, enterprises need infrastructure to run them securely and reliably at scale, without giving up control of their data, systems, or models. We're building open, Kubernetes-native infrastructure that brings together agent execution, secure access to tools and systems, and centralized controls for identity, permissions, and policy. This is an opportunity to help shape a foundational layer for enterprise AI while the architecture is still being defined.

We build in the open alongside the community. Our open source projects include ToolHive, an MCP platform that secures more than 20 million tool calls each month, and Mecatl, a cloud-native agent harness. Our commercial offering, Stacklok Enterprise, extends these capabilities with an AI gateway, centralized identity, policy enforcement, and observability.

Location

This is a remote role based in North America, with a strong preference for candidates located in the U.S. Eastern Time Zone
.

The Opportunity

AI agents are moving into production, and the harness that runs them is becoming critical infrastructure. Enterprises need that harness to be secure, auditable, and portable across models, clients, and deployment environments. Mecatl is Stacklok's open source, cloud-native agent harness. It provides the agent loop, tools, permissions, hooks, delegation, and durable sessions for running agents as production workloads on infrastructure you operate.

As a Software Engineer II on the Mecatl team, you will build the platform that agents run on, and you will build it with agents. This is a hands-on role with real independence. You will deliver features and fixes across the engine, the Kubernetes-native runtime, the client surfaces (gRPC, HTTP/SSE, the TypeScript SDK, and the terminal client), and the permission and governance layers that make agent behavior safe to trust. You will go deep in one area while developing a system-wide understanding of how the harness fits together.

We are also an AI-first engineering team. We use agents throughout our own development lifecycle, and we are still working out what good looks like. Your own experiments, and what you learn from them, will feed directly into how the team works.

What Success Looks Like: First 3-6 Months

Ramped quickly on the Mecatl codebase and its development process, and began contributing independently without needing close guidance.
Shipped your first features and fixes within the first few months, then delivered core harness work consistently thereafter.
Owned a product-minded improvement end to end, from understanding how people use Mecatl to shipping a change and learning from the result.
Contributed a concrete improvement to how the team uses AI in development, such as a workflow, evaluation, guardrail, or measurement approach that the team adopted.
Strengthened the team and community by reviewing pull requests thoughtfully, including AI-assisted changes, and helping open source users get more from Mecatl.

In This Role, You Will

Build and deliver features in the open across Mecatl, including the agent loop, tool and permission systems, session and state management, the Kubernetes runtime, and client SDKs.
Fix bugs and harden the harness for production use, improving reliability, security, and observability.
Write testable, readable code that accounts for edge cases and error handling, produce clear design docs for the work you take on, and review pull requests, including AI-assisted changes.
Understand outcomes and partner with the team anchor to break down the work. Escalate decisions to product or staff engineers as needed.
Use AI agents as a core part of your own workflow, and bring a critical eye to what they produce: review it, test it, and own it.
Find where your AI workflow breaks down on Mecatl work, experiment to fix it, and bring structured findings back so the team gets faster and better, not just busier.
Apply security judgment to AI-assisted development, including permissions, secrets handling, untrusted content, and the limits of what an agent should be trusted to do.

Desired Skill & Experience

We do not expect every candidate to meet every point below. If this role excites you and you bring most of it, we encourage you to apply.

Proficiency in Go, writing clean, testable code that accounts for edge cases and error handling, plus clear design docs and thoughtful code reviews.
Demonstrated ability to deliver features independently across a backend or platform codebase, from implementation through testing and into a release.
Working knowledge of distributed systems and cloud-native infrastructure, such as Kubernetes, containers, and service APIs (gRPC or HTTP). Experience with durable state, concurrency, or streaming is a plus.
A personal AI-assisted development workflow you can walk through, with a clear sense of where it helps, where it breaks, and its risks, such as prompt injection and excessive agent permissions.
Interest in agent infrastructure, such as agent loops, tool use, MCP, model providers, or evaluation. Prior experience building on or contributing to an AI platform or open source project is a plus.
Ideally, a product engineering mindset: curious about users and their problems, comfortable questioning requirements, and motivated by shipping something people use.
AI-first mindset: builds AI into the development workflow to accelerate delivery, improve the quality of what ships, and rethink how problems get solved.
Communication: excellent written and verbal communication, able to explain complex technical ideas clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
Startup mentality and intrinsic motivation: self-directed and hands-on, thrives in fast-moving, ambiguous environments, and drives clarity through action.

Compensation:
The anticipated base salary range for this position is $157,500 - $192,500
. In addition to base salary, this role offers equity and a comprehensive benefits package.

Why Join Us?

At Stacklok, we believe great technology is built by teams that support, challenge, and inspire one another. We are AI maximalists, confident in AI's potential and committed to building technology people can trust. We use AI in our own work and experiment openly.

You'll build alongside people with deep experience in open source, cloud-native technologies, security, and developer tools. We stay close to customers, use our own products, and share what we learn to keep improving. You'll have room to make decisions, support when you need it, and teammates who push themselves to do their best work.

We offer competitive compensation and equity, comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, and a flexible hybrid or remote work environment. Our benefits include flexible PTO, paid holidays, and paid parental leave, along with team offsites to collaborate and connect in person.

If you're excited about what we're building and want to work with people who care about their craft, community, and each other, we'd love to hear from you.

Our dedicated team members are building the future of Cisco’s AI-driven platforms and data infrastructure, supporting innovation across the globe. Your Impact

You are a passionate software engineer with expertise in developing scalable data pipelines, designing robust analytics platforms, and building infrastructure to support machine learning initiatives. Your strong background in programming, data systems, and collaboration enables you to solve complex challenges with innovation and attention to detail. By building and maintaining key software tools and platforms, you enable Cisco’s business groups to leverage AI and data-driven insights for operational excellence and strategic growth. Your work ensures high-quality, reliable data infrastructure that supports Cisco’s leadership in intelligent, scalable technology solutions. 

Minimum Qualifications 

Meet one of the following (completed within the past 3 years or expected to be completed within the next 12 months): 
A Master's degree with 0 years of work experience; or 
A Bachelor's degree with 2 years of work experience; or

Qualifying education and work experience should be in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Cybersecurity, IT, or a related program.   
Proficiency in Python or another programming language, with a strong understanding of software engineering fundamentals, including data structures, algorithms, and object-oriented programming.  
Foundational knowledge of data analysis, machine learning, artificial intelligence, or related concepts, gained through coursework, projects, research, internships, or other hands-on experience.  
Familiarity with data technologies and tools, such as SQL, data processing frameworks, machine learning libraries, or cloud platforms, with the ability to learn and apply new technologies. 

Preferred Qualifications 

Hands-on experience with AI/ML.   
Familiarity with major cloud platforms, such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud.

Familiarity with distributed data processing and containerization/orchestration technologies, such as Apache Spark, Hadoop, Apache Flink, Docker, or Kubernetes.

Why Cisco?

At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.

We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

Experience with Object Oriented Design and Development
