jobs.title: Software Engineer — Reverse Engineering & Legacy Integrations
jobs.description:
About Psyrin

Psyrin builds AI for behavioral health. Our voice agent, Mira, runs the clinical interviews around a behavioral health visit: intake, consent, screening, and a structured psychiatric pre-assessment. It then drafts the assessment and treatment plan documentation for the clinician to review and sign.
Across our partner clinics, Mira has given clinicians 3.3× the assessment capacity per hour of manual assessment (as of September 2026). Psyrin is live with multiple behavioral health organizations, most of them community mental health and addiction providers, as well as work with state government. Our work serves Medicare and Medicaid patients, some of the most vulnerable populations in America.
The company was founded by doctors, psychologists, and AI researchers, largely from King's College London. We're published in Nature and backed by top thesis-driven investors.
While others build surface-level apps, we dig deep into the root causes of psychiatry's problems: inconsistent assessment quality, subjective diagnoses, and fragmented measurement systems. By capturing not just what patients say but how they say it, we're working toward our long-term vision: democratizing access to psychiatric evaluation and building precision psychiatry with AI. In short, an AI psychiatrist, built with the scientific rigor that mental healthcare demands.

The role

We're building an AI platform for mental healthcare, and we're looking for an exceptional engineer with experience reverse-engineering undocumented APIs and building connectors between legacy enterprise systems and modern applications.
We want someone who loves figuring out how complex software works from the outside, can reverse-engineer black-box behaviour, and turn their discoveries into reliable, production-grade integrations.

The challenge

We integrate with legacy Electronic Health Record (EHR) platforms, many built over 20 years ago on Oracle/PL-SQL, Microsoft SQL Server, and other legacy enterprise backends.
Behind these internal application APIs are complicated stored procedures, hidden server-side session state, inconsistent validation, and limited transactional guarantees.
We build Chrome browser extensions that use an authenticated user's session to interact with the same APIs used by the official EHR web application. A seemingly simple operation, such as creating a patient or saving a clinical note, can involve 10 or more dependent API calls.
The hardest part is not making the happy path work (although that isn't always easy). It's anticipating everything that could go wrong.
Without documentation or vendor support, you'll be responsible for proactively identifying and mitigating failure scenarios across long, stateful chains of operations: partial writes, unexpected server state, concurrency, duplicate records, interrupted requests, and subtle data-integrity issues. You'll need to reason about what the system might be doing internally, test your hypotheses, and design integrations that fail safely when assumptions don't hold.

What we're looking for

Real experience reverse-engineering software interfaces and building working integrations against undocumented APIs is our strongest requirement.
We're particularly interested in engineers who have built connectors into legacy systems by investigating how their existing applications communicate with their backends, rather than consuming officially supported, documented APIs.
Relevant experience might include:
Online travel booking:
Automating booking portals, travel-agent applications, or complex GDS workflows, particularly through reverse-engineered APIs, browser extensions, or browser-based automation.
Payroll and HR connectivity:
Building integrations into payroll providers or workforce platforms through undocumented web interfaces.
Insurance:
Automating legacy carrier portals, quoting systems, policy administration, or claims workflows.
Banking and financial connectivity:
Reverse-engineering online banking interfaces, account aggregation, or complex financial transaction workflows.
Other legacy enterprise software:
Building unsupported connectors, automation, or interoperability layers for complex, stateful applications.

The scale or commercial success of the project matters far less than what you personally figured out and built. Relevant experience could come from a substantial hobby project, an independent experiment, a one-person commercial product, or an engineering team.
You'll also need:
Strong JavaScript/TypeScript, HTTP, browser, and modern web application fundamentals.
Experience or strong familiarity with Chrome extensions, browser APIs, and session management.
Exceptional analytical reasoning, resourcefulness, and an ability to infer complex system behaviour from limited evidence.
Deep attention to correctness, concurrency, partial failures, and data integrity.
The ability to produce maintainable software while moving exceptionally quickly.
Proactivity and agency.
To be comfortable and happy with full ownership over integration.
Strong passion towards mental health and the company's mission.
Strategic planning around design and ability (or strong willingness) to anticipate diverse user behaviors.
Almost obsessive enthusiasm and interest in your field of work with the strong, continuous desire to improve.
To be comfortable with an early stage, high-velocity, quickly changing start up environment and work independently with minimal managerial oversight.
To have the ability to reflect, admit your mistakes, own them, learn from them and bounce back stronger.
To care - about your work, impact and colleagues.
Willingness to learn HIPAA requirements and handle protected health information carefully.
Able to travel to the US for business when needed.

How we work

We are a high-velocity engineering team. Our ambition is to build, in months, integrations that would traditionally take years to deliver in healthcare.
We're looking for someone who combines deep technical curiosity with urgency and execution. Someone equally comfortable with modern application architecture and the messy realities of legacy enterprise systems, who challenges assumptions, experiments rapidly, and finds creative ways around difficult technical constraints without compromising correctness.
We expect you to be highly proficient with modern AI-assisted engineering tools, using them to accelerate research, reverse engineering, implementation, testing, and iteration while independently validating their outputs.
We believe software engineering is changing fundamentally. We want someone who recognises that change, embraces emerging tools and techniques, and wants to help define what highly effective software engineering looks like over the next few years.
We care about exceptional ability, demonstrated ingenuity, agency and what you can actually build - not job titles, credentials, or years of experience.

Location and travel

Based in the San Francisco Bay Area or London. We'll also consider candidates elsewhere in the UK or US who can travel to San Francisco or London regularly.
We meet in person for a team retreat once a quarter.
You must already have the right to work in the UK or the US, and be able to travel to the US for business when needed.

Compensation and benefits

A competitive base salary, depending on experience and location.
An equity grant.
Benefits: unlimited PTO and quarterly in-person team retreats for everyone; in the US, 100% of premiums paid for PPO Platinum (or equivalent) health insurance plus dental and vision, a safe harbor 401(k) with a 3–5% employer match, one round-trip flight home a year, and Groundfloor membership for Bay Area staff; in the UK, a Revolut Ultra subscription and a NEST workplace pension. Full details on our careers page.
All work travel costs covered.

How to apply

Send your CV to careers@psyrin.ai with a short note on why you want to build in psychiatry and behavioral health, and how Psyrin's mission fits with yours.
Psyrin is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every background and don't discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

Our engineers design and develop all aspects of the ground communications systems including the Radio Frequency (RF) microwave optics and feeds, cryogenic low noise amplifiers, high power RF transmitters, digital receivers, mechanical/structural elements of large antennas and antenna construction, and precision antenna pointing utilizing advanced servo controllers.

* High proficiency in Java and database experience.
* Deep knowledge of Python and Bash scripting for tooling, system administration, and troubleshooting.
* Experience with kernel configuration and cross-compilation toolchains for embedded architectures.
* Familiarity with Docker containerization for development and build environments.
* Familiarity implementing cybersecurity requirements in software systems.

* Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to work effectively as part of a small, collaborative team.

**DESIRED SKILLS**

Quantum Space is redefining mobility and maneuverability in space. Our high-mobility spacecraft platforms support national security, civil, and commercial missions with unmatched flexibility and propulsion capability. We build fast and iterate quickly.

**Who We're Looking For**

We are seeking a highly skilled Spacecraft Ground Software Engineer III to lead the development, integration, and operational support of software systems that enable spacecraft testing, mission operations, and real-time ground communications.

This role is ideal for an experienced software engineer who thrives at the intersection of distributed systems, mission operations, infrastructure, and real-time data processing. You will play a key role in building the software platforms and operational tooling that support spacecraft integration, command and telemetry workflows, and mission readiness throughout the vehicle lifecycle.

You will work closely with flight software, AI&T, mission operations, avionics, and systems engineering teams to develop scalable and reliable ground software solutions that support both integration and on-orbit operations.

**Where You'll Make an Impact**

* Lead design, development, and deployment of ground software components including payload data pipelines, telemetry processing, event handling, dashboards, tool development, and automated monitoring.
* Own major portions of the ground segment architecture and guide long‑term technical direction.
* Develop tools and automation to improve reliability, operator efficiency, and system observability across satellite missions.
* Work with mission operators, mission design and analysis, and systems engineering to understand operational workflows and translate them into software solutions.
* Lead integration of new spacecraft, subsystems, and communication interfaces into the ground system.
* Implement scalable microservices, APIs, and data pipelines to support real-time and offline mission operations.

* Support anomaly investigations by building diagnostic tools, analyzing telemetry flows, and identifying root causes within the ground architecture.

* Bachelor's degree in computer science, electrical engineering, aerospace engineering, software engineering, or a related technical field.
* 5+ years of software engineering experience, including production experience developing complex systems.
* Strong proficiency in at least one major programming language (Python, Go, C++, or Java).
* Experience developing distributed systems, APIs, or microservices architectures.
* Familiarity with cloud platforms, containerization (Docker), and orchestration frameworks (Kubernetes).

**Nice-to-Have Experience**

* Contributions to system architecture decisions, scaling strategies, and infrastructure automation.

**What You'll Get**

* Ownership – Lead the development of mission-critical ground software that supports spacecraft integration, testing, command and telemetry, and on-orbit operations from concept through deployment.

jobs.title: Embedded Flight Software Engineer
jobs.description:
**Company Description**

Proteus Space is a Los Angeles-based spacecraft technology company established to capitalize on a rapidly evolving space landscape and the urgent need to deliver resilient orbital capabilities to maintain and increase our national science and security interests. We combine serious space flight experience with an open minded, first-principles approach, leveraging advanced computational design and Industry 4.0 practices to deliver custom spacecraft and mission solutions with industry leading speed, precision, and reliability. We seek to enable every payload and mission with a fully custom, purpose-built spacecraft bus, designed and delivered using Proteus™, our patent-pending, automated computational design platform, with industry leading reliability.

**Role Description**

We are seeking an Embedded Flight Software Engineer with deep expertise in low-level embedded software, FPGA interfaces, drivers, and bootloader development to join our flight program team. This is a full-time, in-office role for an experienced professional with a proven track record of hands-on FSW development. In this role, you will design and implement low-level drivers, BSPs, and boot systems while managing memory architectures and FPGA hardware interfaces. You will bridge the gap between low-level hardware and high-level FSW logic, ensuring reliable spacecraft boot behavior, fail-safe recovery, and deterministic bus communications in space environments.

**Key Responsibilities**.

* Develop low-level C/C++ drivers, Board Support Packages (BSPs), and hardware interfaces for microcontrollers, FPGAs, and standard communication buses.
* Design and implement stage-1 and stage-2 bootloaders, robust boot behaviors, partition swapping logic, and fail-safe recovery modes.
* Architect memory management strategies across volatile and non-volatile memory (NOR/NAND Flash, SRAM, EEPROM) to preserve data integrity across reboots.
* Configure low-level communication protocols and bus interfaces (e.g., SPI, I2C, CAN, UART, SpaceWire, or PCIe) between compute units, peripherals, and payloads.
* Implement telemetry collection, time synchronization, and task scheduling within RTOS or embedded OS environments.
* Execute hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing and debugging on flatsats using logic analyzers, oscilloscopes, and FPGA emulator tools.
* Manage the codebase using modern version control systems and contribute to CI/CD workflows for automated testing and continuous integration.
* Execute comprehensive test campaigns on testbeds and flight units to verify software performance under flight-like conditions.
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate subsystems with the spacecraft main compute element.
* Ensure compliance with industry standards and regulatory requirements.
* Document design processes, test results, and system performance.
* Provide technical guidance on FSW architectures to fellow engineers, fostering a culture of excellence and innovation.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's or advanced degree in computer science, aerospace engineering, or similar field.
* 5+ years of embedded software engineering experience, with exposure to low-level driver development, hardware integration, or bootloaders.
* Strong proficiency in C, C++, embedded Linux, and Real-Time Operating Systems (RTOS).
* Familiarity with version control systems (e.g., Git) and automated testing/CI workflows.
* Strong ability to collaborate effectively in a dynamic environment while maintaining a positive and professional attitude.
* Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
* Must possess or be willing and eligible to obtain a United States Department of Defense Top Secret security clearance.

**Desired Qualifications:**

* Experience writing custom drivers for FPGA logic blocks or hardware interfaces (such as I2C, CAN, SPI, UART, or SpaceWire).
* Experience with hardware-level communication protocols and hardware/software integration.
* Experience working in clean room environments and adhering to ESD protocols.
* Demonstrated experience with custom bootloader design, memory controller drivers, Flash file systems, and image verification/recovery techniques.

**Salary Range:** $130,000 - $180,000 per year. Final compensation is based on experience, education and qualifications.

**Benefits**

Proteus Space offers comprehensive benefits including paid medical healthcare for employees, flexible vacation policy, sick days, 401k matching option, pregnancy leave, family leave, holiday pay, military service leave, dental care, vision care and other benefits.

**Equal Opportunity**

Proteus is committed to providing equal employment opportunities regardless of an applicant's age, disability, sex, race, religion, gender, national origin, veteran status or any other legally protected characteristic. The Company will provide reasonable accommodations to an applicant with a disability or religious belief in or to enable the applicant to apply for the position.

As a Quality Automation Engineer at Infotech, you'll help ensure the quality, reliability, and performance of the products that state transportation agencies, contractors, and local governments rely on every day. You'll join a fast-paced development team and own how we test, from the framework that runs the checks to the standards that shape how the whole engineering organization thinks about quality.

### **Who we are looking for**

You have strong experience with test automation frameworks, API testing, and CI/CD pipelines, and you feel most at home in an agile environment. You design test suites that are scalable and maintainable, and you can tell a flaky test from a true product bug at a glance. You understand the business your tests protect.

  

You're also a collaborator. You'll partner with engineers and product managers early, during refinement, to define acceptance criteria and build for testability, and you'll help developers add automated checks earlier in the pull request cycle. You're curious about how AI tools and new techniques can improve how we deliver software, and you're passionate about building quality from the start.

We build software that makes our customers' jobs easier, faster, and less complicated. We do this by learning their challenges, solving problems in thoughtful ways, and always looking for ways to improve.

This opportunity is particularly well-suited to someone early in their software development career, including recent graduates or developers with approximately zero to three years of professional experience. We're looking for someone with a strong technical foundation, a willingness to learn, and the curiosity to grow into a well-rounded engineer.
  
You'll write real code that ships to real users, with support from experienced engineers who will help you develop your skills through code reviews, pairing sessions, and day-to-day mentorship.

**What’s in it for You?:**

**Compensation:**

GovCIO is hiring a Frontend Developer to build and modernize federal applications on a serverless AWS GovCloud stack. The developer starts with a focus on frontend work and is expected to grow into a full-stack role.

This position is remote within the Continental United States (CONUS).  
  
**Job Description**  
A GovCIO Frontend Developer works inside a cross-functional product team with designers, backend developers, DevOps engineers, and test engineers. The developer builds and maintains modern web applications using JavaScript, React, and Redux, integrating them with REST APIs on a serverless AWS backend. Strong skills in JavaScript patterns and practices, frontend frameworks, and CSS/SASS are essential. The role is hands-on and deadline-driven. Work starts and finishes inside the sprint. The developer works from user stories and designer wireframes, builds accessible and secure user interfaces, and understands how the frontend and serverless backend fit together. This Frontend Developer position is expected to grow into a full-stack developer role, building backend services with Python and AWS serverless technologies such as API Gateway, Lambda, and Step Functions. At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

Affirm is building the next generation of customer identity and authentication. This role is a hands-on, mid-engineering position inside Information Security, contributing to core CIAM capabilities that protect customers and support growth.

You will help build and maintain backend services that power registration, login, authorization, and account lifecycle flows across B2C and B2B experiences. You will work with experienced engineers and partner teams to deliver scoped identity features with strong security fundamentals, reliability, and operational rigor.

### **What you'll do**

* Build and ship customer-facing authentication features—from smoother login experiences to MFA, step-up authentication, and device binding—with mentorship from experienced engineers.
* Develop backend services and APIs in Python or Kotlin, turning product requirements into working software that helps customers access their accounts securely.
* Work with modern identity technologies such as Okta, Auth0, and ForgeRock, writing custom code and integrations that connect identity capabilities to web, mobile, and partner applications.
* Take scoped features through the software development lifecycle: contribute to design, write readable code and automated tests, participate in code reviews, and deploy to production with support from the team.
* Solve real engineering problems by debugging services, improving reliability, and using logs and metrics to understand how your code behaves in production.
* Collaborate with engineering and product partners, learn secure development practices, and grow your software engineering skills while building expertise in authentication.

  

### **What we look for**

We're looking for a Mid-Level Software Engineer with solid engineering fundamentals, a passion for authentication, and an eagerness to learn customer identity and access management. You do not need extensive authentication or CIAM experience—we value your ability to build software, solve problems, and grow in the space.

* Demonstrated ability to write, test, and debug software in Python, Kotlin, or a similar language through coursework, internships, personal projects, open source, or professional work. No fixed minimum years of experience required.
* Foundational understanding of backend development, including APIs, data structures, databases, and version control.
* Genuine curiosity about how authentication works and motivation to build secure, reliable customer experiences. Prior experience with identity protocols or CIAM platforms is a plus, not a requirement.
* A practical problem-solving approach, willingness to ask questions, and openness to learning through mentorship and code review.
* Clear communication and the ability to collaborate with engineering, product, and security teammates.

Title

NS4R Software Developer

At KBR, we deliver science, technology and engineering solutions to governments and companies around the world. KBR employs approximately 37,000 people worldwide with customers in more than 85 countries and operations in over 28 countries. KBR is proud to work with its customers across the globe to provide technology, value-added services, and long-term operations and maintenance services to ensure consistent delivery with predictable results.

Trinzic is the future independent company to be created through the planned spin-off of KBR's Mission Technology Solutions business, expected in January 2027. Our people work at the frontier of what is possible, delivering solutions in challenging environments and advancing some of the world's highest-priority national security and space missions. 

Backed by decades of mission success, deep expertise, and trusted partnerships, Trinzic will launch as a global organization with more than 18,000 employees supporting customers around the world. Join us at a defining moment and help shape the future of a company built to tackle complex challenges and make a meaningful impact. 

Candidates who join KBR's Mission Technology Solutions business before the spin-off will transition to Trinzic when the separation is complete and will not need to reapply for employment. 

Job Summary

KBR is seeking an NS4R Software Developer to join our team in Colorado Springs, CO or El Segundo, CA.

This job supports SSC within the Joint Terminal Engineering Office (JTEO) as a developer on the National Security SATCOM Systems Synchronization Roadmap (NS4R) software application. The NS4R application is hosted on Defense Information Systems Agency’s (DISA) MilCloud and requires close coordination with DISA to resolve issues in a timely manner. In support of JTEO, duties include maintaining the NS4R database including security upgrades, development and implementation of enhancements to the NS4R tool, providing user held desk support, maintaining user accounts, providing NS4R database backups, maintaining configuration control and backups of the source code, support JTEO to evaluate and address security requirements and perform troubleshooting. The job requires the ability to assist Level 1 POCs with data entries and identify and correct incomplete or questionable data entries and management of the NS4R MilCloud Virtual Data Center (Memory/Storage/CPUs etc.). This also includes development and installation of patches to the Operating System and Data Base Server. As needed, you can expect to train Government and FFRDC personnel on the use and maintenance of the NS4R tool and database.

The MILSATCOM Systems Engineering, Integration, and Test (MSEIT) effort provides leading edge Systems Engineering & Integration (SE&I) for the Air Force’s Space and Missiles System Center. We support the Air Force’s acquisition of state-of-the-art Military Satellite Communications systems, providing global secure, survivable, and protected communications for our nation’s warfighters. We seek technical individuals who will thrive in a highly collaborative work environment of small teams, using the most modern tools and methodologies to tackle the challenges of integrating complex space and ground communications systems.

Required Experience

Active Secret clearance required for this position
Bachelor's degree in a STEM field
Experience working with military or DOW civilian clients and managing professional relationships
Strong interpersonal skills, communication (oral and written), and presentation skills
Capable in Microsoft Office products (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
2+ years of experience across the following software suites: Angular, Java, Microservices, Docker, DISA Stratus, VMWare

Preferred Experience

5+ years of experience across the following software suites: Angular, Java, Microservices, Docker, DISA Stratus, VMWare
2+ years of experience in SATCOM
INCOSE CSEP or ESEP certification

Work Environment

Location:
On-site

Minimal

Standard, 40 hours per week (Full-time)

Compensation

For Colorado Springs, CO only, the salary range for this position is approximately $94,000 - $117,400. For El Segundo, CA only, the salary range for this position is approximately $102,900-$128,600. The offered rate will be based on the selected candidate’s knowledge, skills, abilities and/or experience and in consideration of internal parity.

Other Compensation

KBR may offer bonuses, commissions, or other forms of compensation to certain job titles or levels, per internal policy or contractual designation. Additional compensation may be in the form of sign on bonus, relocation benefits, short term incentives, long term incentives, or discretionary payments for exceptional performance.

KBR Benefits

KBR offers a selection of competitive lifestyle benefits which could include 401K plan with company match, medical, dental, vision, life insurance, AD&D, flexible spending account, disability, paid time off, or flexible work schedule. We support career advancement through professional training and development.

Ready to Make a Difference?

jobs.description:
Overview

Job Description:

We don’t simply hire employees. We invest in them. When you work at Chatham, we empower you — offering professional development opportunities to help you grow in your career, no matter if you've been here for five months or 15 years. Chatham has worked hard to create a distinct work environment that values people, teamwork, integrity, and client service. You will have immediate opportunities to partner with talented subject matter experts, work on complex projects, and contribute to the value Chatham delivers every day.

Chatham Financials' Summer Internship Program offers a dynamic and immersive experience for aspiring technology professionals. This is your opportunity to gain hands-on software engineering experience in a leading finance and technology firm while contributing to projects that drive our business forward.

As a Software Engineering Intern at Chatham, you will be immersed in a collaborative team environment where you'll work alongside experienced engineers on cutting-edge products. Whether you're developing new features, optimizing systems, or solving complex problems, you'll play a key role in shaping the future of finance through technology.

Our technology team is made up of a team of Software Engineers, Testers, DevOps Engineers, Security Engineers, UX Designers, Quantitative Analysts and Data Base Analysts. We build software for our clients that range across multiple sectors and industries as well as tools for our internal users to help them better serve our clients. Our team is a global team located in four different countries and multiple time zones. We interact daily with each other as well as our key business stakeholders to ensure quality and speedy delivery of our product offerings.  

What You’ll Do

"Use AI workflows and AI coding assistants as peers and collaborators to help you deliver the best technology solutions for Chatham"
Assist with developing cutting-edge financial applications; develop innovative, high-quality, and robust web applications and micro services as part of our growing application development team. 
Be a member of an agile scrum team that owns development of a specific product or platform. 
Collaborate with other software engineering teams, design team, quant team, product owners and managers, and business stakeholders, while working on intern project. 
Develop software in our technology stack which is constantly evolving but currently includes .NET,  ASP.NET, React, Angular, TypeScript, SQL Server, RabbitMQ and Redis. 
Build automated unit, integration and front-end tests using xUnit, Moq, NSubstitute and Cypress among other technologies. 
Implement the build, test, deploy development cycle in CI/CD pipelines using Docker, YAML, Gitlab CI, and Hashicorp Nomad
Use AI workflows and AI coding assistants as peers and collaborators to help you deliver the best technology solutions for Chatham

What You’ll Need: 

Working towards Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience. 
2 years of experience preferred
Experience with object-oriented languages such as C#, C++ or Java 
Experience with JavaScript and JavaScript frameworks (e.g. React) 
Experience with relational databases such as Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle or MySQL 
Understanding of Unit testing, Test-Driven Development and mocking frameworks 
Understanding of continuous delivery principles and processes 
Understanding of REST principles, Service-oriented architecture, and API development 
Understanding of continuous delivery principles and processes 
Proclivity towards refactoring and continuously improving OO code through agile development methods. 
Open-source development projects. 
Contributions to the local developer community. 
Quantitative and modeling skills with an ability to learn techniques in numerical optimization, data mining, simulation, or model calibration. 

This role offers flexibility and is eligible for a hybrid work arrangement.

Chatham Financial offers an entrepreneurial culture that rewards teamwork and innovation. We seek individuals who are natural leaders, quick learners, and fit our collaborative culture. Join us to develop your fullest potential, impact our clients and community, and kickstart your career in finance.

Apply now and become a part of Chatham Financial's legacy of excellence and innovation!

Applicants must be enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate academic program at the junior or senior level.

Implement well-scoped tasks and projects across our stack, including Java and Python services hosted in Kubernetes and Snowpark Container Services, with input from other team members.
Learn to engage in all aspects of the software lifecycle, from design through supporting the deployment.

Collaborate within a cross-functional team, including product management and design.

jobs.title: UI/UX Software Engineer - NREC
jobs.description:
At the National Robotics Engineering Center (NREC), it is our engineers and technicians who drive the breakthroughs that define our success. The members of our technical staff collaborate closely with leadership and multidisciplinary teams to design, build, and deploy sophisticated robotic solutions that address complex challenges in industrial, commercial and government sectors. Each project benefits from their expertise, creativity, and hands-on problem-solving, fueling progress and innovation across the organization.

As part of our dedicated team, you will work alongside world-class robotics professionals committed to pushing the boundaries of technology and redefining ideas into solutions for real-world applications. We foster a culture of professionalism, respect, and collaboration, offering a flexible and encouraging environment where you can sharpen your skills, lead impactful projects, and take control of your career development.

We are seeking a dynamic UI/UX Software Engineer for existing and new projects. In this position, you will work on a variety of user interfaces for robotic systems. You will have an opportunity to collaborate on an internal team and with sponsoring partners to support the work through all lifecycle stages. Our team has members with diverse backgrounds both in robotics and other industries aligned to make robust software and firmware that is useful in the world. Projects you may support range from industrial machine operator assist systems to agricultural productivity tools and beyond to other automation, autonomy, or safety systems. Your day-to-day work will include developing user interfaces for internal and external usage centered around robotic systems.

Your Primary Responsibilities Include

Co-Design Human-Machine Interfaces: Partner closely with robotics engineers, hardware teams, and field operators to design custom, intuitive interfaces for complex robotic systems.
Build Native Qt/QML Frontends: Develop fluid, hardware-accelerated user interfaces using QML and/or Qt, binding them smoothly to backend C++ or Python data streams.
Prototype & Test with Real Users: Prototype interaction flows and collaborate directly with end-users to evaluate usability, safety, and operator performance in the field.
Integrate Real-Time System Data: Connect UI components to central system state engines, telemetry feeds, and databases while ensuring the interface remains fast and responsive.
Champion Collaborative Software Development: Actively participate in an inclusive team culture through constructive peer reviews of both designs and code, integration testing, version control, and clear documentation.
Integrate & Adapt APIs: Adapt open-source libraries, proprietary tools, and backend APIs to extend UI capabilities cleanly and maintainably.
Cross-Functional Field Testing: Validate and refine interfaces through hands-on testing with both simulated environments and physical robotic hardware alongside the broader engineering team.

Required Qualifications

Education & Experience: B.S. in Computer Science, HCI, Design, or equivalent practical experience, with 1–3+ years of combined academic or professional software development experience.
Qt / QML Proficiency: Hands-on experience building modern, responsive user interfaces using QML and/or Qt.
Frontend-to-Backend Integration: Understanding of how to connect QML frontends to application backends (via C++ signals/slots, PySide6/PyQt, or async data handlers).
User-Centered Mindset: Ability to translate user feedback, operational workflows, and rough sketches/wireframes into clear, functional visual layouts.
Teamwork & Communication: Strong interpersonal and technical communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to thrive in a cross-functional, multidisciplinary team environment.
Core Engineering Standards: Proficiency with Git version control, writing clean code, and participating in peer code/design reviews.
Adaptability & Curiosity: Enthusiasm for learning how physical hardware works and bridging the gap between human operators and complex machines.

We especially want to hear from you if you have experience or qualifications in ANY of the following areas:

Experience designing for touch pendants, handheld controllers, or embedded/cyber-physical systems.
Experience with robotics frameworks or tools (ROS / ROS 2, Gazebo, or 3D telemetry visualization).
Experience conducting usability interviews or observing end-users operating hardware in the field.
Exposure to Python, backend development, or database integration.
Familiarity with graphic design tools (Figma, Adobe XD, GIMP, or Photoshop) or Qt Design Studio.
Experience with Android development or embedded Linux deployment.

Other Requirements

Successful pre-employment background check

This position will require work on a variety of projects, including projects that involve military/defense applications and/or are funded by military/defense sponsors.

Are you interested in joining our versatile team at NREC where you will have a direct impact on operations and meaningful projects?

Join a collaborative environment where your hands-on skills, leadership, and mentorship will directly influence operations and inspire the next generation of innovators.

Why NREC?

At NREC, you will shape the robotics revolution by tackling real-world challenges in agriculture, manufacturing, defense, energy, and much more. You will work alongside top robotics experts, develop ground breaking technologies, and see your solutions deployed in the field.

NREC At a Glance

Located in Pittsburgh or “Roboburgh”, a hub for over 120+ robotics companies
30+ years of pioneering robotics research
150+ professionals driving innovation and real-world impact
Part of Carnegie Mellon University’s Robotics Institute, a global leader in robotics

NREC also leads in educational outreach through its Robotics Academy, which develops curricula and software for K–12 and college-level students. You will also have opportunities to engage with these student groups through outreach activities.

As part of our team, you will have the flexibility to grow your career - whether becoming a technical expert, leading projects, mentoring others, or exploring new pathways and making an impact in developing technologies that drive progress, improve safety and transform industries.

Joining the CMU team opens the door to an array of exceptional benefits.

Benefits eligible employees enjoy a wide array of benefits including comprehensive medical, prescription, dental, and vision insurance as well as a generous retirement savings program with employer contributions. Unlock your potential with tuition benefits, take well-deserved breaks with ample paid time off and observed holidays, and rest easy with life and accidental death and disability insurance.

Additional perks include a free Pittsburgh Regional Transit bus pass, access to our Family Concierge Team to help navigate childcare needs, fitness center access, and much more!

For a comprehensive overview of the benefits available, explore our Benefits page.

At Carnegie Mellon, we value the whole package when extending offers of employment. Beyond credentials, we evaluate the role and responsibilities, your valuable work experience, and the knowledge gained through education and training. We appreciate your unique skills and the perspective you bring. Your journey with us is about more than just a job; it’s about finding the perfect fit for your professional growth and personal aspirations.

Are you interested in an exciting opportunity with an exceptional organization?! Apply today!

jobs.description:
Company Overview
At Skild AI, we are building the world's first general purpose robotic intelligence that is robust and adapts to unseen scenarios without failing. We believe massive scale through data-driven machine learning is the key to unlocking these capabilities for the widespread deployment of robots within society. Our team consists of individuals with varying levels of experience and backgrounds, from new graduates to domain experts. Relevant industry experience is important, but ultimately less so than your demonstrated abilities and attitude. We are looking for passionate individuals who are eager to explore uncharted waters and contribute to our innovative projects.
Position Overview
We are seeking a Software Engineer to own the software that provisions, calibrates, and tests our robots, from the manufacturing line through service and repair. Your goal: every robot that leaves the line or comes back from repair works as a complete system, and technicians can verify it without engineering help. You will own escalations from manufacturing and service: you triage, dig in, fix what's yours, and drive cross-team resolution when it's not. Your work means engineers and researchers can trust the robots they use, so model evaluations reflect the model, not a faulty robot.
This is a hands-on role at the point where hardware, firmware, and software come together. Alongside building test software, you will turn recurring failures into lasting product and process improvements. You will work closely with manufacturing, hardware, firmware, perception, and robotics teams, as well as the technicians who build and repair our robots.
Responsibilities
Build automated manufacturing tests that verify each robot is fully functional before it leaves the line, with results tracked for each robot.
Turn engineering scripts for provisioning, flashing, and calibration, such as camera calibration, into guided workflows technicians can run.
Build one-click service tests that let technicians verify a robot is fully repaired before handing it back.
Build startup self-checks that verify each robot's hardware, software versions, and configuration every time it boots.
Define pass/fail criteria with the hardware, perception, and controls teams that own each subsystem.
Root-cause test failures across hardware, firmware, and software, and drive fixes with the owning teams.
Track failure modes and repeat issues, and feed learnings back into design, assembly, and test processes.

Preferred Qualifications
BS, MS or higher degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Minimum of 3 years of industry experience.
Proficiency in Python and C++.
Experience writing software that interfaces with real hardware, such as motors, sensors, and embedded devices.
Experience building automated tests, manufacturing test stations, or technician-facing test tools.
Comfort debugging across hardware and software, including reading schematics and working with communication buses like CAN or EtherCAT.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Privacy & Data Governance
jobs.description:
We're looking for an engineer to help manage how data is handled across Thinking Machines: what we collect and acquire, where it is stored, who and what systems can access it, how long we keep it, and how it's used in training, evaluation, and products. You'll help build the systems that let us protect privacy and make definitive statements about our practices from data inventory and classification through access and purpose controls to retention, deletion, and audit. You'll also collaborate closely with researchers and product engineers to answer privacy questions that don’t have textbook answers.

This is a role for someone who knows privacy deeply and treats it as an engineering problem rather than a checklist. The questions we face are rarely settled by policy alone: what it means to honor a deletion request against a trained model; how customers' fine-tuning data on Tinker should be isolated, never commingled, and only used for the customer; when to deidentify data (and how) vs. apply differential privacy to it. We want someone who can weigh privacy against model quality, research velocity, and product usefulness, pick a defensible answer, and then build it.

What You'll Do

Implement and enforce privacy and data governance across internal systems day to day by building systems like data classification tagging, retention jobs, deletion pipelines, and data classifiers and integrating them across systems at Thinking Machines.
Build the isolation guarantees that keep customer and user data separate and protected, including the training data customers bring to Tinker and the conversations people have with our interfaces.
Run privacy reviews and threat models on new data sources, training runs, and product features, and close them out by shipping the control, the check, or the tooling, not only a recommendation.
Translate legal and policy requirements (GDPR, CCPA, contractual commitments) into working code: policy-as-code, CI checks, and pipeline enforcement, built and maintained by you.
Maintain shared libraries and guardrails that make the private path the default, and fix them when they break or fall out of date.

Skills and Qualifications

Minimum qualifications
Built and shipped at least one production privacy or data governance system (retention/deletion pipeline, policy evaluation engine, data cataloging and/or lineage system, consent system, or similar) and owned it through to operation, not just design.
Written and operated production code in Python or a comparable language, evidenced by a system you can walk through in detail: what it does, how it fails, how you debugged it.
Direct experience with enforcing privacy or governing data in an AI/ML data pipeline (training data, fine-tuning, inference, or evaluation) and can describe a specific privacy risk you identified or mitigated in one of these systems.
Has chosen pragmatic controls over ideal ones on real systems, and can describe what was shipped as a result.
Has written a technical requirement or control directly from a legal or policy obligation (GDPR, CCPA, or similar), and can name the obligation and the control.

Preferred qualifications
Experience at an AI lab or with ML infrastructure: training data curation, multi-tenant fine-tuning platforms, or inference systems that handle user data.
Has implemented a privacy-enhancing technique (deidentification, differential privacy, secure enclaves) in a real system, and can describe where it fell short.
Experience building data lineage, metadata, or policy-engine tooling, or large-scale deletion and retention systems.
Background in security engineering, or has worked directly with a security team on access control implementation.
Has been one of the first engineers building out a privacy function, and can point to the specific systems they personally built, not just the program they ran.

We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.

A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.

As a Software Engineer
in our Creator Services Communication Pod, you will build the next generation communications plane to power the millions of experiences on the Roblox Platform.

To give some examples of what we do, we run the mission-critical Cross-server Messaging Service, which is crucial for Roblox game developers to implement leaderboards, cross-server announcements, live operations and more. We own the developer APIs for HTTP calls to external systems and player teleports within and between game servers. We are also launching Compute Functions, which provide developers with a new surface to execute game logic for more robust features such as custom matchmaking, limited inventory drops, or any background task processing. To tie features like these together, we are building a general Game Server Management product to unify developers' observability and control of their servers.

At its core, this team is focused on solving complex back end distributed systems and networking problems at scale. However, our scope extends to full stack projects spanning all the way from the infrastructure layer, through engine development, data pipelines, microservices, telemetry, game servers, web development, UI, and UX design. This team collaborates on multiple cross-company efforts and our projects are of extremely high importance to Roblox. If you enjoy working on modern distributed systems, products for developers, C# and C++ software, and networking challenges alongside highly-experienced and passionate engineers, you will be right at home on our growing Creator Services team.

You Have

2+ years of professional software engineering experience, with strong ownership working in complex technical systems.
Knowledge: You are comfortable working with systems level programming languages (C++, C#, Objective C, Rust, or similar programming language).
Curiosity: You are eager to work across a wide range of systems and understand the Roblox ecosystem end to end
Long-term Mindset: You are considerate of how your work impacts the team/users over time, not just getting the green checkmark on a deliverable

You Will

You will develop new products and features that help creators make complex experiences including live game operations at many-million-player scale.
You will support core systems at massive scale including how players move between game servers, how game servers communicate with each other, and how experiences interact with on and off platform services.
You will work across the technology stack such as the C++ game engine, Kafka streams, Flink jobs, Elasticsearch/Redis/Clickhouse databases, C# backend services, and React UIs.
You will take ownership of projects throughout their full lifecycles.

Emerson's Test & Measurement business helps engineers solve some of the world's most complex challenges through industry-leading test, measurement, and analytics solutions. jobs.title: Robotics Software Engineer, Autonomy
jobs.description:
Join Us, and Ship Robots

Weave was founded to build the robots we’d want to have in our own home. We believe the next generation of robotics will transform everyday life by enabling people to do more and to reclaim time to spend on what’s important.

We also believe robots are in a sense like any other product: to matter, they have to ship. Our robots are already operating in real homes and businesses, giving us the opportunity to rapidly improve from real-world experience. With a growing team, strong customer demand, and capital for expansion, we’re entering an exciting stage of growth—and we’re looking for people with exceptional talent and standards to help bring home robotics to millions of households.

The Role

Weave is building robots that work in real customer homes. We’re looking for a software engineer with strong robotics fundamentals who enjoys developing algorithms, designing systems, and making them work on physical machines. You’ll develop software for localization, motion planning, and autonomy, with a role in the architecture that connects these capabilities. The work spans mathematical modeling, algorithm development, sensor integration, and system validation. You should enjoy making thoughtful design decisions and following an idea from its formulation through implementation and measured performance on a robot.

We value strong fundamentals, practical judgment, and curiosity across disciplines. You might bring years of experience developing robotic systems, or a smaller set of substantial projects that demonstrate depth and resourcefulness. There’s room to investigate new methods and deepen your expertise, with success measured by what our robots can reliably do.

What You'll Do

Localization and state estimation: Develop algorithms that combine IMUs, cameras, wheel odometry, and other measurements to estimate robot motion and maintain reliable localization.
Trajectory analysis and motion planning: Analyze robot trajectories and develop planning algorithms that account for geometry, kinematics, obstacles, and execution constraints.
System architecture and validation: Make system-level decisions about computation, timing, data flow, and component responsibilities. Define metrics and validation methods to assess accuracy, latency, robustness, and overall behavior.
AI and autonomy: Assess research in AI and robotics, evaluate emerging autonomy architectures, and integrate promising approaches where they improve robot capabilities and reliability.
Sensors and hardware: Integrate and characterize sensors, manage calibration and synchronization, and understand how hardware limitations and environmental conditions affect algorithm performance.
Software architecture: Design maintainable C++ and Python software, clear interfaces, and reliable communication across the robotics stack, using ROS 2 and other frameworks or custom infrastructure as appropriate.

What You'll Bring

Hands-on robotics experience: You’ve implemented and tested algorithms on physical systems and worked through the gap between a clean formulation and imperfect hardware.
Strong mathematical foundations: You’re comfortable with linear algebra, coordinate transformations, probability, and numerical optimization. You can reason about uncertainty, assumptions, and failure modes.
Depth in a core robotics discipline: Substantial experience in state estimation, sensor fusion, SLAM, motion planning, trajectory optimization, or control, with an interest in learning adjacent areas.
Algorithmic understanding: You understand the principles behind the methods you use. Relevant experience might include Kalman or particle filtering, factor graphs, bundle adjustment, graph search, constrained optimization, or model predictive control.
Strong software engineering: Experience implementing algorithms in C++, using Python or similar tools for experimentation and analysis, and contributing to maintainable software within a team.
Experimental judgment: You can design an informative experiment, compare results against ground truth or other meaningful references, and distinguish an algorithmic limitation from an integration or sensor problem.
Curiosity and ownership: You’re willing to investigate unfamiliar parts of the system and carry a problem through to a tested solution.

Nice To Have

Experience integrating multiple sensor modalities, including cameras, IMUs, wheel encoders, LiDAR, or radar.
Experience with sensor characterization, calibration, system identification, or parameter estimation.
Experience deploying algorithms under onboard compute, power, or latency constraints.
Familiarity with ROS or ROS 2.
Experience with mobile robots or mobile manipulators.
Experience evaluating learned methods for perception, estimation, or planning.

You don’t need experience in every area listed. We’re interested in the systems you’ve built, the fundamentals you understand deeply, and how you approach problems you haven’t solved before.

jobs.description:
Overview

Keysight is at the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. Our ~16,800 employees create world-class solutions in communications, 5G, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets for customers in over 100 countries. Learn more about what we do.

Our award-winning culture embraces a bold vision of where technology can take us and a passion for tackling challenging problems with industry-first solutions. We believe that when people feel a sense of belonging, they can be more creative, innovative, and thrive at all points in their careers.

We are excited to announce that we are looking for a talented individual to join our team as a Configure, Price Quote (CPQ) Knowledge Engineer (KE) & Application Development Intern. In this role, the candidate will be assisting with the development and maintenance of Product Configuration applications (e.g., Logik.AI), ensuring seamless integration with our existing systems, and optimizing the configuration and pricing processes. We are seeking someone with strong technical skills, a keen eye for detail, and a passion for innovation. If you are looking for an opportunity to work in a dynamic and collaborative environment, we would love to hear from you!

Knowledge Engineers (KEs) collaborate cross-functionally with Marketing, R&D, Order Fulfillment, and Order Management to design ERP product structures and configurations for new product/option introductions with selectable features and pricing. KEs are responsible for automating the generation of accurate product quotes and orders for customers quickly and efficiently, improving quote and sales efficiency. KEs ensure that product configuration complexity is hidden using logical rules to display only relevant product selections and feature information in compliance with product specifications and Keysight Standards, guiding Keysight customers, sales representatives, and field engineers through product selection and configuration.

In the KE Team we also develop applied solutions for streamlining & modernizing digitized processes within Technology Order Fulfillment (TOF), replacing manual processes with innovative informatics and software solutions to increase configuration and operations productivity.

Responsibilities

Primary Responsibilities:

Design new ways to optimize and improve the product quote-to-order process and experience.
Reduce new product introduction time to market through innovative product structure, configuration and related processes or solutions.
Deliver and maintain Technology Order Fulfillment (TOF) software solutions for configuration and operations which complement Keysight Enterprise Solutions.
Drive increased efficiency and productivity.
Modernize existing processes and digital assets with a focus on reducing or replacing manual work and eliminating waste.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications:

Pursuing a BS in Computer Engineering, Computer Science or equivalent degree
Proficient with standard Microsoft Office suite (e.g., Excel, Outlook, MS Word, etc.)
Good oral and written communication skills
Experience with web application development
Experience with object-oriented programming

Desired Qualifications

Experience using Microsoft Visual Studio
Working knowledge of the Angular framework or a similar framework, such as React
Understanding of REST APIs and CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations
Experience with Atlassian tools, including Confluence, Jira, and Bitbucket
Knowledge of relational databases, SQL, or T-SQL
Ability to analyze data using applications such as Power BI, report builder, or other data visualization tools.

The level of role will be based on applicable experience, education and skills; most offers will be between the minimum and the midpoint of the salary range listed below.

CA pay range: MIN $32.03 to MAX $34.49

Note: for other locations, pay ranges will vary by region.

Relocation is available for this position.

jobs.title: Software Engineer - New Grad, Distributed Data Systems (2027 Start)
jobs.description:
P-965

At Databricks, we are obsessed with enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems, from security threat detection to cancer drug development. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform, so our customers can focus on the high value challenges that are central to their own missions.

Our mission at Databricks is to radically simplify the whole data lifecycle from ingestion to ETL, BI, and all the way up to ML/AI with a unified platform. To achieve this goal, we believe the data warehouse architecture as we know it today will be replaced by a new architectural pattern, Lakehouse (CIDR 2021 paper), open platforms that unify data warehousing and advanced analytics. The new architecture will help address several major challenges, including data staleness, reliability, total cost of ownership, data lock-in, and limited use-case support.

As part of this team, you could be working in one or more of the following areas:

Query compilation and optimization
Distributed query execution and scheduling
Vectorized execution engine
Data security
Resource management
Transaction coordination
Efficient storage structures (encodings, indexes)
Automatic physical data optimization
Data plane storage
Storage management system

What We Look For

You will graduate in Fall 2026 or Spring 2027 with a degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related subject
You have implementation skills with a general purpose program language, such as Java, or C++
You have knowledge of algorithms, data structures, and OOP principles
A passion for database systems, storage systems, distributed systems, language design, or performance optimization
You have experience managing end-to-end projects

PACCAR is a Fortune 500 company established in 1905. PACCAR Inc is recognized as a global leader in the commercial vehicle, financial, and customer service fields with internationally recognized brands such as Kenworth, Peterbilt, and DAF trucks. Today, Kenworth is leading transportation innovation with the introduction of battery-electric vehicles, exploration of fuel cell electric powertrains, and autonomous driving systems. Kenworth is committed to fostering an environment of diversity, equality and inclusivity in the workplace.

The North American Materials organization is seeking a motivated Data Engineering Intern to join our IT team in Chillicothe, OH.
This internship provides an opportunity to gain hands-on experience supporting supply chain operations and data-driven decision making. The intern will work with experienced team members to help develop data solutions, support reporting initiatives, and learn modern data engineering tools and technologies. This role offers valuable exposure to data warehousing, cloud technologies, analytics, and business intelligence within a global manufacturing environment.

Learn first-hand from experienced data engineers and analytics professionals.
Gain exposure to enterprise data warehousing and cloud-based technologies.
Participate in real-world projects supporting supply chain and business operations.
Develop mentoring relationships with experienced professionals.
Build technical and professional skills through hands-on project work.

Support the development and maintenance of data warehouse and reporting solutions.
Assist with data integration and ETL/ELT processes from multiple business systems.

Collaborate with Data Engineers, Data Analysts, and business users on data-related projects.
Assist in creating dashboards, reports, and visualizations using business intelligence tools such as Power BI and Tableau.
Support database and cloud platform activities involving technologies such as Snowflake, SQL Server, AWS, and other enterprise systems.
Participate in documenting data processes, business requirements, and technical solutions.
Contribute to process improvement initiatives through data analysis and problem solving.

Qualifications

Demonstrated interest in data engineering, analytics, data science, or information technology.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

Excellent communication and organizational skills.
Strong attention to detail and willingness to learn new technologies.

Preferred Skills

Basic knowledge of SQL and relational databases.

Familiarity with Python or other programming languages.

Ally Financial only succeeds when its people do - and that’s more than some cliché people put on job postings. We love this stuff! We see our people as, well, people - with interests, families, friends, dreams, and causes that are all important to them. Our focus is on the health and safety of our teammates as well as work-life balance and diversity and inclusion. From generous benefits to a variety of employee resource groups, we strive to build paths that encourage employees to stretch themselves professionally. We want to help you grow, develop, and learn new things. You’re constantly evolving, so shouldn’t your opportunities be, too?

Work Schedule:
Ally designates roles as (1) fully on-site, (2) hybrid, or (3) fully remote. Hybrid roles are generally expected to be in the office a certain number of days per week as indicated by your manager. Your hiring manager will discuss this role's specific work requirements with you during the hiring process. All work requirements are subject to change at any time based on leader discretion and/or business need.

The Opportunity

Provides contributions in the design, coding, testing, support and debugging of new software or enhancements to existing software.

The Work Itself

Contribute to software engineering efforts to deliver well-defined products that generate immediate customer value and deliver high-quality, broadly applicable software contributions.
Participate in agile ceremonies to scope, plan, and commit to a backlog for delivery.
Participate in DevOps principals practiced by the engineering organization.
Collaborates with other Engineers, Technical Leads, Architects, QA, Performance Testers, Scrum Masters, and Product Owners.
Uses technical knowledge, creativity and company practices and priorities to obtain solutions to complex problems.
Interfaces with senior management to provide and obtain information and to build consensus regarding project direction.
Escalate issues to senior management early, before they create significant impact to a project/release.
Review and approve all mid-level design documentation.
Ensure that detail design documentation is competed, reviewed, and approved, as required.
Conduct or participate in code review sessions to ensure quality and performance.
Participate and contribute to innovation workshops and hackathons
Support the system integration and user acceptance testing resources. Provide timely defect analysis, remediation, and reporting.
Review security testing reports/results and remediate potential vulnerabilities in a timely manner.
Serves as a mentor to lower level developers.
Interacts directly with business clients.

The Qualifications We’re Looking For

1+ years of applicable experience and a bachelor’s degree in technical discipline, or an equivalent combination of experience and education.
Knowledge of all phases of software development including design, coding, testing, debugging, implementation, and support
Experience writing and reviewing software design specifications in an object-oriented development environment
1+ years on experience with Robocorp and Python programming, which is commonly used with Robocorp.
Object oriented programming with Microsoft .Net (VB and C#) or VBA, Java Scripting, Python
Familiarity with web service interaction (JSON/XML)
Strong use of Microsoft Office productivity tools including, Excel, Word, Access, PowerPoint
Strong Problem-Solving and Analytical Skills
Effective communication skills for technical and non-technical audiences
Strong written and verbal communications skills
Understanding and ability to work under varying project delivery methodologies (Agile, Waterfall)
Proficient understanding of code versioning tools such as GIT.
Experience translating product requirements into design specifications.
Debugging and problem-solving skills.
Ensure quality software is delivered with minimal defects and no go live critical issues. Knowledgeable of unit and automation testing tools.
Ability to thoroughly understand the business issues surrounding each project
Ability to respond directly to questions from business clients
Ability to be a technical authority and work with other team members
Knowledge of standard change management tools and processes
Ability to work in a team environment
Hands on technical experience

Minimum Qualifications

1+ years of experience
High school Diploma or GED equivalent

How We'll Have Your Back

Ally's compensation program offers market-competitive base pay and pay-for-performance incentives (bonuses) based on achieving personal and company goals. Our Total Rewards program includes industry-leading compensation and benefits plus additional incentives that are designed to meet your needs and those of your family so you can get the most out of your career and your life, including:

Time Away:
Program starts at 20 paid time off days in addition to 11 paid holidays and 8 hours of volunteer time off yearly (time off days are prorated based on start date and program varies based on full or part-time status and management level).

Planning for the Future:
plan for the near and long term with an industry-leading 401K retirement savings plan with matching and company contributions, student loan pay downs and 529 educational save up assistance programs, tuition reimbursement, employee stock purchase plan, and financial learning center and financial coach access.

Supporting your Health & Well-being:
flexible health and insurance options including medical, dental and vision, employee, spouse and child life insurance, short- and long-term disability, pre-tax Health Savings Account with employer contributions, Healthcare FSA, critical illness, accident & hospital indemnity insurance, and a total well-being program that helps you and your family stay on track physically, socially, emotionally, and financially.

Building a Family:
adoption, surrogacy and fertility assistance as well as paid parental and caregiver leave, Dependent Day Care FSA back-up child and adult/elder care days and childcare discounts.

Work-Life Integration:
other benefits including Mentally Fit Employee Assistance Program, subsidized and discounted Weight Watchers® program and other employee discount programs.

Other Compensations:
depending on the role for which you are considered, you may be eligible for travel allowances, relocation assistance, a signing bonus and/or equity.

To view more detailed information about Ally’s Total Rewards, please visit this link: https://www.ally.com/content/dam/pdf/corporate/ally-total-rewards-snapshot.pdf

Ally Financial is a customer-centric, leading digital financial services company with passionate customer service and innovative financial solutions. We are relentlessly focused on "Doing it Right" and being a trusted financial-services provider to our consumer, commercial, and corporate customers. For more information, visit www.ally.com.

Description

Recognized as the No. 1 site trusted by real estate professionals, Realtor.com® has been at the forefront of online real estate for over 25 years, connecting buyers, sellers, and renters with trusted insights and expert guidance to find their perfect home. Through its robust suite of tools, Realtor.com® not only makes a significant impact on the real estate industry at large, but for consumers, navigating the biggest purchase they will make in their life, by providing a user experience that is easy to use, easy to understand, and most of all, easy to make decisions. Join us on our mission to empower more people to find their way home by breaking barriers to entry, making the right connections, and building confidence through expert guidance.
Who are we:
Have an interest in making an impact for millions of consumers? Do you thrive in a cross-collaborative environment? Are you ready to take on your next career challenge? If you want to pursue your professional goals as you help grow an innovative real estate tech company, this work is for you!

We’re offering a dynamic opportunity for an Associate
Software Engineer to join our Owners & Sellers team. In this role, You will act as a foundational technical engineer running mission-critical platforms that directly drive revenue, while taking charge of initiatives that improve the consumer experience and drive core business outcomes. Leverage the latest technologies, including Typescript, React, Node.js, NextJS, GraphQL, AWS, AI tools, and more, to accelerate your professional growth and achieve new heights in your career.

Top Reasons to Apply:
Hands-On Cloud & DevOps Ownership
You’ll own the infrastructure, not just the code. You will design AWS data pipelines and automate the toolchain (using Lambda, ECS, and CloudFormation) to enable instant service provisioning and zero-friction deployments.
AI-Driven Engineering Culture
The team actively rewards engineers who leverage AI tools as a performance multiplier. You’ll be encouraged to use AI to write better code faster and accelerate development in a forward-thinking environment.

What you’ll do:
●    Develop and Maintain: Own systems and evolutions for key parts of the Owners & Sellers platform, defining clear boundaries, contracts, and data models between services. Participate in and lead architectural discussions, contributing to technical design documents and implementation proposals.
●     Full-Stack Excellence: Maintain and improve the stability, readability, and scalability of the codebase, ensuring best practices across backend services and frontend architecture using React and Next.js.
●    Optimize Performance & Reliability: Drive performance improvements and optimize Core Web Vitals (such as INP metrics) across our pages. Lead operational excellence by ensuring services meet SLAs, influencing incident response, and continuously reducing incident volume and MTTR.
●    Leverage Cutting-Edge Tooling: Utilize AI coding assistants and LLMs proficiently to accelerate development velocity, generate boilerplate, and troubleshoot complex debugging scenarios, while exercising critical judgment to verify outputs for security and accuracy.

What You’ll Bring:
●    Software development experience, including internships, academic projects, or relevant professional experience. including time in large-scale, distributed systems 
●    Full-stack proficiency: Experience in frontend web development with a strong focus on Typescript, React js and Apollo GraphQL combined with deep proficiency in backend languages like Node js and GraphQL.
●    AI Tooling Mastery: Proven proficiency using modern AI-assisted SDLC environments and agents (e.g., Claude/Cursor/GitHub Copilot, - based engineering agents) and drive AI adoption at scale
●   Cloud & Infrastructure Expertise: Experience designing and operating cloud-native services on AWS (EKS, containers like Docker, managed databases) with modern CI/CD orchestration (e.g., CircleCI, ArgoCD, Kubernetes).
●    Systems Design: Strong grounding in system design, data modeling, API design, responsive design principles, and CSS technologies like PandaCSS/CSS3.
●    Observability & Data-Driven Mindset: Comfort working with observability tooling (metrics, logs, traces like NewRelic and Splunk) and using data to debug, optimize, and harden production systems.
●    Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science/Engineering/related field or equivalent professional experience.
How We Work:
We balance creativity and innovation on a foundation of in-person collaboration. Our employees work three days in our Austin headquarters where they have the opportunity to collaborate in-person, adding richness to our culture and knitting us closer together.
How We Reward You:
Realtor.com® is committed to investing in the health and wellbeing of our employees and their families. Our benefits include:
●        Inclusive and Competitive medical, Rx, dental, and vision coverage.
●        13 Paid Holidays and Flexible Time Off.
●        Immediate eligibility into Company 401(k) plan with 3.5% company match.
●        Family forming benefits and Student Debt Retirement Savings Match program.
●        Tuition Reimbursement and 1:1 personalized Financial Planning Sessions.
●        8 hours of paid Volunteer Time off.
●        Free snacks and refreshments in each office location.
Realtor.com® is an Equal Opportunity Employer regardless of age, color, national origin, race, religion, creed, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, marital status, or disability status.
